jobs.title: VP, Impact and Operations
jobs.description:
NeighborWorks as a Company and an Employer

For nearly 50 years, Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation, a congressionally chartered national nonprofit known as NeighborWorks® America, has strived to make every community safer and more prosperous. Our network of excellence includes nearly 250 nonprofits in every state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and on Native lands. NeighborWorks offers grant funding, peer exchange, technical assistance, evaluation tools, and access to best-in-class training as the nation’s leading trainer of housing and community development professionals. NeighborWorks network organizations build homes and apartments, expanding the supply of affordable housing in every community; provide financial counseling and coaching that increases self-sufficiency; encourage resident leadership; and collaborate with local stakeholders in the areas of health, economic development, employment, and education.

Caring for communities starts with caring for our internal community, our staff. Picture yourself in a collaborative and diverse hybrid environment surrounded by colleagues who challenge, encourage and inspire you. This opportunity offers an impressive total rewards package that includes a 401(k) match of up to 12%, 11 paid holidays, generous leave (including 40 hours of paid volunteer time) and industry-leading benefits. Start your career with NeighborWorks America and take advantage of our Staff Training and Education Program (STEP), designed to support continued learning and professional development. Our benefits are designed to support staff holistically, enabling them to give their best in both work and life.

We are a mission-based organization committed to building a high-performing work culture, guided by the following core values:

  • We hold ourselves and each other accountable.
  • We act with integrity.
  • We lead with curiosity.
  • We pursue excellence with courage.
  • We respect, honor and celebrate each other.
  • We collaborate with purpose.

Work at a Glance: Drive Grants, Performance, and Change

Position Summary:

The Vice President, Impact & Operations provides strategic leadership for the Field Operations Division's grants administration, operational effectiveness, performance management, organizational learning, and change management functions. The position leads the division's Impact & Operations team and is responsible for establishing the policies, processes, and systems that support effective execution of division priorities and stewardship of corporate resources. As a member of the division's leadership team, the Vice President serves as a strategic advisor on organizational effectiveness and change management in support of the division's goals, service to the NeighborWorks network, and engagement with key stakeholders

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

1.Executive Leadership and Team management

-Participates fully as a critical member of the division’s leadership team in support of Field Operations Division strategies and goals.

-Leads the Field Operations Division Impact & Operations team, including direct supervision of Director, Grants Management, Director, Finance & Operations, and Project Manager, responsible for the division’s grantmaking, budgeting, procurement, purchasing, events planning/management, administrative support, and project management.

-Supports a “team of teams” approach within the Impact & Operations team and with colleagues across the Field Operations Division, to ensure shared expectations, goal-setting, and accountability in grants administration, operations, and project management.

2.Grant Administration, Fiscal Stewardship & Governance

-Oversees corporate grants administration, including management of the corporation’s approximately $95 million federal funds grants budget, and oversees grant-making activities for grant opportunities led by the Field Operations Division and works collaboratively with other divisions participating in the grant-making process.Assists the Senior Vice President in representing the grant processes and programs to internal and external stakeholders.

-Oversees budget activities for the Field Operations Division budget, including the federally appropriated grants fund budget.

-Maintains a system of regular review and updates of corporate policies, procedures, and relevant staff training resources relating to processes led by the division, including grants, affiliations, disaffiliations, and the NeighborWorks network charter agreement; including supervising staff responsible and collaborating with relevant internal and network stakeholders.

-Oversees the division's operational technology interfaces and business systems, including collaboration with Information Technology Services (ITS) and management of key internal and external platforms that support grants administration, performance management, operations, and service delivery.

3.Organizational Performance, Learning & Continuous Improvement

-Leads the development and implementation of strategies to intentionally support a system of reflection, evaluation, identification & capturing learnings, codifying tools, and enabling feedback loops to support a learning culture within the division, in partnership with division leadership.

-Directs and supervises the development, evaluation and revision of performance measures relating to the corporate, division, and department level scorecards for the Field Operations division.

4.Strategic Planning & Change Leadership

-Advises the Senior Vice President and colleagues across the division in effective change management practices to inform strategies and implementation across the division.

-Serves as a strategy resource for NeighborWorks network organizations to be tapped by network management team.

5.Cross-functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement

-Collaborates closely with cross-divisional leadership of Finance, Financial Planning/Analysis/Contracts, Procurement, National Initiatives, Organizational Assessment, Evaluation Leadership & Peer Learning, Training, Public Policy & Legislative Affairs, and Corporate Strategy & Impact in support of corporate goals for responsible fiscal stewardship of resources, grantmaking, and service to the NeighborWorks network.

-Assists the Senior Vice President in representing the grant processes and programs to internal and external stakeholders.

6.Performs other duties as assigned.

·Oversees teams responsible for division’s operations and grantmaking, including three direct reports.

·Collaborates closely with the division’s leadership to ensure operational needs are met in a way that supports mission

·Collaborates closely with leadership and staff of the corporation’s Finance and Administration divisions in overseeing the division’s budgeting, procurement, purchasing, grantmaking, and change management efforts.

·Collaborates closely with NeighborWorks Office of General Counsel in overseeing regular updates of corporate policies within the division’s areas of responsibility.

·Collaborates closely with programmatic teams recommending grants.

Fiscal Responsibilities:

·Oversees the division’s procurement, and purchasing to ensure the division’s work is done in alignment with corporate fiscal policies and within the available budget.

·Oversees the division’s annual operating budget of approximately $800,000-$900,000

·Oversees the corporation’s annual consolidated grants budget of approximately $95 million of federal funds

Required Minimum Qualifications:

(b) Experience:

·Minimum of 12-15 years of progressively responsible experience in budget, finance, operations, grants administration, nonprofit leadership, and/or a related field.

jobs.title: Merchant Support Associate, Entry Level
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Our teams work closely across product, engineering, customer success, sales, and company leadership to bring new capabilities to market and continuously improve the platform.

At Bask, we value people who take initiative, enjoy helping entrepreneurs, and are willing to learn how our software works. Our customers include people building and operating their own businesses, and we believe clear communication, reliable support, and strong follow-through make a real difference in their experience.

About the Role

We're looking for a Merchant Support Associate, Entry Level to help entrepreneurs and businesses using Bask Health with routine software questions, platform navigation, and everyday support needs.

This is an entry-level, customer-facing position designed for someone who wants to develop experience in SaaS customer support, e-commerce technology, and merchant operations.

You'll help customers understand how to use supported platform features, troubleshoot common issues, and find the right resources when they need assistance.

You'll work closely with Customer Success Managers, technical support specialists, and other internal teams to ensure merchant questions are handled accurately.

Bask Health provides software that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform connects merchant storefronts, patient questionnaires, checkout experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy-related processes, and other business capabilities.

You'll learn how merchants use the platform to operate their businesses.

You'll develop an understanding of the merchant-facing software workflows relevant to your responsibilities.

You'll respond to routine merchant support requests through approved communication channels.

You'll help customers navigate their accounts and locate supported platform features.

You'll provide approved guidance on basic storefront, questionnaire, and checkout-related questions.

You'll help merchants understand where to find relevant settings, instructions, and support resources.

You'll follow established troubleshooting procedures when customers encounter common software problems.

You'll ask clarifying questions to understand what a merchant is trying to accomplish.

You'll gather relevant information when a customer reports an issue.

You'll document the problem clearly and accurately.

You'll help distinguish between routine navigation questions and issues requiring specialized technical assistance.

You'll escalate complex problems to technical support or customer success engineering teams.

You'll provide relevant information so the receiving team can investigate efficiently.

You'll communicate approved updates to merchants when a support request remains unresolved.

You'll follow up on assigned support tickets according to established procedures.

You'll help ensure customers understand the next steps for resolving their questions.

You'll avoid making unsupported promises about software functionality, fixes, or timelines.

You'll maintain accurate records of merchant interactions and support requests.

You'll use approved ticketing, CRM, or customer support systems.

You'll organize assigned tickets and follow-up tasks.

You'll track open requests and help prevent issues from being overlooked.

You'll learn how to categorize and prioritize customer support requests.

You'll follow established procedures for escalating urgent or sensitive concerns.

You'll communicate professionally with entrepreneurs and business owners.

You'll remain patient when assisting customers who are unfamiliar with the software.

You'll explain platform steps clearly without unnecessary technical language.

You'll recognize that customers may have different levels of experience with e-commerce and software tools.

You'll adapt your communication style to help each merchant understand the information being provided.

You'll help customers locate onboarding resources, tutorials, and support documentation.

You'll assist with routine onboarding questions when appropriate.

You'll coordinate with Customer Success Managers when a request relates to a customer's broader account relationship.

You'll help identify customers who may need additional onboarding or product education.

You'll document recurring merchant questions and share them with the support team.

You'll contribute to internal troubleshooting guides and frequently asked questions.

You'll help identify unclear instructions that may be causing repeated support requests.

You'll provide feedback about common customer difficulties.

You'll participate in training on new platform features and support procedures.

You'll learn how different parts of Bask Health's software interact.

You'll become familiar with common merchant workflows and configuration questions.

You'll develop practical knowledge of online storefronts, checkout processes, and e-commerce operations.

You'll learn how entrepreneurs use software to manage their businesses.

You'll work with more experienced team members to understand complex support situations.

You'll ask questions when a customer request falls outside your knowledge or authority.

You'll apply feedback to improve your communication and troubleshooting skills.

You'll gradually become more confident handling routine support requests independently.

You'll help maintain consistent support quality by following established procedures.

You'll work with Customer Success Managers to understand how support issues can affect customer satisfaction and retention.

You'll coordinate with technical teams when a software issue requires deeper investigation.

You'll learn how support tickets are documented and escalated to engineering.

You'll help identify when a reported issue may affect multiple merchants.

You'll report suspected widespread platform problems through approved channels.

You'll avoid independently making technical changes outside your authorized responsibilities.

You'll follow approved privacy, security, and information-handling procedures.

You'll access only the customer information necessary and authorized for assigned tasks.

You'll use designated systems when communicating or documenting customer information.

You'll recognize and report suspected privacy or security concerns.

You'll recognize when a customer question involves clinical, pharmacy, or compliance matters.

You'll direct those questions to the appropriate licensed or authorized teams.

You'll never provide medical advice, make clinical decisions, or promise prescription-related outcomes.

You'll maintain a professional and helpful approach when customers are frustrated.

You'll focus on understanding the issue rather than making assumptions.

You'll take responsibility for assigned support requests and follow through on commitments.

You'll manage multiple routine questions while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.

You'll communicate proactively when you need help or additional information.

You'll stay organized when balancing support tickets, follow-up tasks, and training responsibilities.

You'll be comfortable working with a remote team and communicating through online collaboration tools.

You'll contribute to a team environment that values initiative, accountability, and continuous learning.

You'll help identify small improvements that make support processes more efficient.

You'll support the creation of clearer customer instructions and internal documentation.

You'll develop practical skills in SaaS support, merchant communication, and basic technical troubleshooting.

You'll learn how Customer Success and Support teams work together to help merchants succeed.

You'll build experience working directly with entrepreneurs and growing businesses.

You'll understand how reliable customer support contributes to a positive merchant experience.

You'll be encouraged to take ownership of your work while asking for guidance when needed.

We're looking for someone who is organized, dependable, comfortable using software, and genuinely interested in helping customers.

You don't need years of professional support experience, but you should communicate clearly, learn quickly, and be willing to work through problems.

Experience in retail, customer service, e-commerce, online business operations, or a relevant internship would be helpful.

Personal experience running an online store or working on an entrepreneurial project would also be valuable.

Success in this role means resolving routine merchant questions accurately, maintaining organized support records, escalating complex issues appropriately, and steadily developing stronger customer support skills.

What You'll Do

  • Respond to routine merchant support requests through approved channels.
  • Help merchants navigate Bask Health's platform.
  • Assist with basic account and software navigation questions.
  • Provide approved guidance on supported storefront workflows.
  • Help customers understand basic questionnaire and checkout-related functionality.

  • Report suspected widespread technical issues through approved channels.
  • Follow privacy, security, and information-handling requirements.
  • Escalate clinical, pharmacy, and compliance matters to authorized teams.
  • Communicate professionally with entrepreneurs and business owners.
  • Manage assigned support requests with strong organization and follow-through.
  • Identify opportunities to improve routine support processes.
  • Take ownership of assigned tasks and continue developing customer support skills.

Requirements

  • Entry-level to 1 year of relevant experience in customer support, customer service, retail, e-commerce, or a related customer-facing environment.
  • Strong interest in helping customers and solving problems.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to explain information simply and professionally.
  • Comfortable learning and navigating web-based software.
  • Basic understanding of customer service principles.
  • Ability to follow established troubleshooting and support procedures.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to document customer questions and follow-up tasks accurately.
  • Willingness to learn customer support ticketing systems and internal tools.
  • Ability to ask clarifying questions when information is incomplete.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and willingness to investigate issues.
  • Ability to recognize when a request requires escalation.
  • Professional and respectful communication skills.
  • Ability to remain calm when assisting frustrated customers.
  • Comfortable working with email, spreadsheets, and online collaboration tools.
  • Ability to manage multiple assigned tasks and support requests.
  • Willingness to learn about e-commerce and online merchant operations.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating with a remote team.
  • Strong accountability for assigned responsibilities.
  • Willingness to receive feedback and apply it to improve performance.
  • Understanding of the importance of privacy and secure information handling.
  • Ability to follow established support and communication procedures.
  • Availability to collaborate during required U.S. Eastern Time working hours.
  • Comfortable working in a growing software company with evolving processes.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in a customer support or customer service role.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including other developers, administrators, and QA testers, to ensure successful project delivery.

  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior team members, fostering a culture of knowledge sharing and continuous learning.

No supervisory/management authority

  • Knowledge of Salesforce integration patterns and technologies, including REST and SOAP APIs.
  • Experience with development projects using DevOps, Salesforce configuration, and/or Apex.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex requirements into efficient solutions.

•U.S. Citizenship required.

  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a Government Public Trust Clearance.
  • Must pass pre-employment qualifications of Cherokee Federal.

jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Content Designer, AI Experiences to help shape how users interact with AI-powered capabilities across Bask Health's software platform.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform brings together merchant tools, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce capabilities.

As we explore and develop AI-assisted product experiences, clear communication becomes essential. Users need to understand what an AI feature can do, what information it uses, when its output may be incomplete, and which decisions remain their responsibility.

As a Content Designer, AI Experiences, you'll design the language and conversational patterns that make AI-powered functionality understandable, useful, and appropriately transparent.

This is a hands-on product content role combining UX writing, conversational design, interaction design, content strategy, and cross-functional product development. You'll work with product designers, product managers, engineers, and AI-focused technical teams to create content for AI-assisted workflows.

Your work may include AI-powered assistants, suggested actions, generated summaries, guided configuration experiences, automated recommendations, and other intelligent product capabilities as they are developed and approved.

You'll help define how AI features introduce themselves, explain their capabilities, ask for information, present results, communicate uncertainty, and guide users toward appropriate next steps.

You'll also design content for situations where AI cannot complete a task, produces an incomplete result, needs clarification, or requires human review. These experiences should help users understand what happened without creating unnecessary confusion or implying capabilities the system does not have.

A major part of this role will involve creating clear boundaries between AI assistance and user decisions. You'll help design messaging that distinguishes suggestions from completed actions, makes important limitations visible, and supports review before consequential changes.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll need to pay particular attention to privacy, accuracy, and appropriate clinical boundaries. You'll collaborate with relevant stakeholders to ensure AI-related content does not misrepresent medical authority, treatment eligibility, or actions requiring authorized human oversight.

You'll participate throughout the product development process, from early concept exploration and prototype writing through usability testing, implementation, and iteration.

You'll also contribute to reusable AI content patterns, including response structures, clarification prompts, confirmation language, error states, and disclosure guidelines.

You'll use user research, usability feedback, and available product data to evaluate whether people understand AI-generated content and can successfully complete their tasks.

We're looking for someone who enjoys solving new product communication challenges, understands the importance of responsible AI interactions, and can translate technically complex functionality into straightforward, useful experiences.

What You'll Do

  • Design clear, intuitive content for AI-powered features across Bask Health's platform.
  • Write interface copy for AI-assisted merchant and operational workflows.
  • Develop conversational interaction patterns for assistants and guided experiences.
  • Create introductory messaging that explains what AI features can and cannot do.
  • Write prompts, suggested questions, and guided input instructions for users.
  • Design content for AI-generated summaries, recommendations, and suggested actions.
  • Help users distinguish AI-generated suggestions from verified information and completed actions.
  • Create clear explanations for automated processes and AI-assisted workflows.
  • Develop content patterns for uncertainty, incomplete information, and unavailable results.
  • Write clarification prompts that help users provide missing or ambiguous information.
  • Design confirmation messages for actions that require user review or approval.
  • Create recovery messaging for unsuccessful or interrupted AI interactions.
  • Develop appropriate handoff language when human assistance or review is required.
  • Collaborate with product designers on conversational layouts and AI interaction flows.
  • Partner with engineers to understand AI functionality, limitations, and system behavior.
  • Work with product managers to define user expectations and content requirements.
  • Participate in the design of AI-assisted merchant configuration experiences.
  • Help create understandable content for AI-generated business insights and operational summaries.
  • Review AI feature prototypes for clarity, transparency, and usability.
  • Develop reusable writing patterns for AI-related product interactions.
  • Contribute AI content standards to Bask Health's broader design system.
  • Establish consistent terminology for AI features, generated outputs, and automation states.
  • Collaborate with researchers to evaluate user understanding and trust.
  • Test whether users can identify AI limitations and appropriately review suggested actions.
  • Work with clinical and pharmacy stakeholders when AI experiences involve sensitive healthcare workflows.
  • Apply accessibility and plain-language principles to conversational and AI-generated interfaces.
  • Document content decisions, AI interaction patterns, and writing guidelines.
  • Own assigned AI content design projects from initial discovery through implementation and iteration.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional experience in content design, UX writing, conversational design, product writing, or a closely related field.
  • Portfolio or work samples demonstrating content design for digital products.
  • Strong writing, editing, and information organization skills.
  • Understanding of user-centered content design principles.
  • Experience creating interface content for web or mobile applications.
  • Ability to simplify technically complex concepts into clear, actionable language.
  • Experience writing instructions, guidance, error messages, confirmations, and system states.
  • Strong understanding of information hierarchy and interaction design principles.
  • Familiarity with conversational interfaces, AI-assisted products, or automated workflows.
  • Ability to design content that sets clear user expectations.
  • Understanding of transparency and user control in automated experiences.
  • Ability to communicate uncertainty and product limitations without confusing users.
  • Experience collaborating closely with product designers and product managers.
  • Ability to work effectively with software engineers and technical stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with Figma or comparable collaborative product design tools.
  • Understanding of accessibility and inclusive writing principles.
  • Experience maintaining consistent terminology across digital experiences.
  • Familiarity with UX writing guidelines or content design systems.
  • Ability to review prototypes and identify content-related usability problems.

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

Nice to Have

An established organisation is automating its finance close on Redwood, connected to SAP. Redwood Finance Automation runs on the same Redwood platform as RunMyJobs. SAP sold that platform for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and later SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). If you have built on it under any of those names, the experience carries straight across.

What you will work on

The close built as Redwood process definitions: task lists, dependencies, parameters and calendars, including SAP factory calendars. Automated steps that run the SAP FI/CO period-end programs in the background, in the right order and with the right variants. Balance sheet reconciliation, accruals and journal posting automated on the platform. Logic in REL and RedwoodScript where the standard designer does not meet the requirement. The connection to SAP S/4HANA or ECC through XBP and RFC. Unit and integration testing, defect fixing, and support through user acceptance testing. Promotion between environments, cutover and hypercare. Technical documentation and handover to the support team.

What you bring

Hands-on build on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. You built the process definitions or job chains yourself. REL and RedwoodScript. SAP connections through XBP and RFC on at least one live SAP estate. Knowledge of the SAP FI/CO programs that run at month-end and the order they run in. 5 or more years in SAP automation, job scheduling or finance systems engineering.

A migration from SAP BPA or SAP CPS to RunMyJobs. Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). SAP Financial Closing cockpit or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry, including work under SOX or similar audit controls.

jobs.title: Senior Platform Engineer, APIs & Workflow Automation
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Platform Engineer, APIs & Workflow Automation to design, build, and improve the shared services, APIs, and automation infrastructure powering Bask Health's telehealth platform.

You'll work on the systems connecting patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, merchant tools, and external services. Your focus will be creating reliable, reusable infrastructure that makes it easier for our engineering team to build and scale products.

This is a hands-on senior engineering role for someone who enjoys working across different systems, solving complex integration challenges, and designing architecture that other engineers can build upon.

Our engineering stack includes TypeScript, Node.js, AWS, SST, and SQL databases, with technologies such as tRPC, Prisma, and Drizzle used across the platform.

You'll collaborate with product engineers, product managers, and operations teams to identify opportunities for automation, simplify complex workflows, and improve the reliability of shared infrastructure.

We're looking for someone who can independently own major technical initiatives, make sound architectural decisions, and build systems that are secure, maintainable, and scalable.

What You'll Do

  • Design, develop, and maintain shared backend services and APIs used across Bask's telehealth platform.
  • Build reusable infrastructure supporting patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and merchant-facing applications.
  • Develop scalable APIs, application services, and integration patterns using TypeScript and Node.js.
  • Design and implement workflow automation that reduces manual operational work and improves system reliability.
  • Build event-driven services and asynchronous processing workflows using AWS Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, and related infrastructure.
  • Develop and maintain serverless applications using AWS and SST.
  • Design database schemas, data models, and service interfaces for shared platform functionality.
  • Build integrations connecting internal applications, external APIs, and third-party services.
  • Develop reusable authentication, authorization, validation, and configuration patterns.
  • Design workflows that handle retries, failures, duplicate events, and complex state transitions reliably.
  • Improve API performance, system reliability, observability, and operational visibility.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify backend architecture and reduce duplicated functionality across engineering teams.
  • Build internal tools and automation that improve developer productivity and operational efficiency.
  • Collaborate with frontend and product engineers to ensure shared APIs support application requirements.
  • Work with product managers and operations teams to translate complex workflows into technical solutions.
  • Establish engineering patterns and standards for API design, event processing, and shared service development.
  • Lead technical design discussions and evaluate architectural tradeoffs.
  • Review code, provide technical guidance, and help other engineers build reliable integrations.
  • Write automated tests covering complex workflows, integrations, and failure scenarios.
  • Investigate production incidents, identify root causes, and implement durable improvements.
  • Improve logging, monitoring, alerting, and debugging capabilities across shared services.
  • Take ownership of major platform initiatives from architecture and implementation through deployment and production support.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor and Claude Code to accelerate development while independently validating code quality, security, and correctness.
  • Help shape the long-term architecture of Bask's backend platform as the company expands its products and integrations.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including substantial backend or platform engineering experience.
  • Strong proficiency in TypeScript, JavaScript, and Node.js.
  • Experience designing, building, and maintaining production backend services and APIs.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS and serverless application development.
  • Experience with AWS Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, or comparable cloud services.
  • Strong experience with SQL databases, relational data modeling, and database schema design.
  • Experience building third-party integrations, working with webhooks, and designing reliable asynchronous workflows.
  • Understanding of distributed systems, event-driven architecture, message queues, and background processing.
  • Experience designing reusable services, shared libraries, or backend infrastructure used by multiple applications.
  • Ability to design workflows with appropriate retries, idempotency, error handling, and recovery mechanisms.
  • Experience implementing authentication, authorization, API security, and secure data handling.
  • Strong understanding of software testing, debugging, monitoring, and production reliability.
  • Experience improving developer workflows through automation, reusable tooling, or shared engineering practices.
  • Ability to independently own complex technical initiatives from design through production deployment.
  • Experience making architectural decisions and evaluating technical tradeoffs.
  • Familiarity with Git, code reviews, CI/CD, and modern software development practices.
  • Experience collaborating across engineering teams to define technical requirements and shared platform standards.
  • Ability to use AI-assisted development tools effectively while independently validating generated code for correctness, security, and maintainability.
  • Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, and attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with significant ownership and responsibility.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with SST and infrastructure-as-code tools.
  • Experience with Prisma, Drizzle, or tRPC.
  • Familiarity with React, Next.js, or full-stack TypeScript applications.
  • Experience with multi-tenant SaaS platforms or monorepo architectures.
  • Experience building workflow orchestration systems, automation engines, or reusable integration frameworks.
  • Experience developing internal developer platforms, shared SDKs, or engineering productivity tools.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD automation, deployment pipelines, and developer self-service tooling.
  • Experience designing event-driven systems with complex state transitions and multiple external dependencies.
  • Experience with observability, distributed tracing, alerting, and production incident investigation.
  • Experience building healthcare, e-commerce, or subscription-based SaaS platforms.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA, data privacy, or regulated software environments.

  • Experience improving API performance, database efficiency, and system scalability.

  • Experience using Cursor, Claude Code, or similar AI-assisted development tools in production engineering workflows.

jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.title: On-Chain Researcher (Attribution & Monitoring)
jobs.candidate_required_location: Hong Kong, Singapore, United Kingdom, United States
jobs.description:
Company Overview

hermeneutic research is a best-in-class proprietary trading firm. It deploys research-driven discretionary and systematic strategies as well as makes strategic long-term investments. The partners' decade-long history of success in trading and business building and a firm-wide cultural emphasis on alpha generation, open debate, relentless iteration, and teamwork are key to the firm's continued expansion in a challenging market environment that has hamstrung competitors. A hard-wired emphasis on risk management and opportunistic market participation ensure that hermeneutic research will continue its growth trajectory in the coming decades.

Job Overview

We are seeking a crypto-native on-chain researcher to join the research team. You will support our senior researchers with real-time monitoring and attribution, helping the team keep continuous coverage of market-moving on-chain activity.

The core of this role is on-chain attribution and monitoring: identifying who is behind wallets, clusters, and flows, and doing it accurately while handling uncertainty. Accurate attribution underpins everything else we build on top of it, including the charts, alerts, and monitoring workflows the team relies on to interpret market-moving activity in real time.

This is an opportunity for a talented on-chain researcher to work in a highly collaborative environment with access to substantial data, technology and trading infrastructure.

Responsibilities

Attribution & Blockchain Analysis

  • Perform entity attribution, wallet clustering, and transaction graph analysis across account-based and UTXO-based blockchains.
  • Investigate unknown wallets and clusters, weighing the evidence and stating confidence honestly before conclusions are shared.
  • Analyze exchange flows, treasury and insider activity, token unlocks, vesting, and cross-venue capital movement.
  • Investigate unfamiliar protocols, entities, and market events quickly and report what the on-chain data does and does not show.

Real-Time Monitoring & Coverage

  • Monitor on-chain activity and market events in real time for potentially tradeable signals, and escalate them to the senior team.
  • Build and maintain monitoring workflows, dashboards, and alerts for themes and entities of interest.
  • Communicate complex blockchain activity clearly and concisely to researchers and traders, including under time pressure in volatile markets.
  • Provide coverage and backup for senior researchers when colleagues are out.

Research Support & Tooling

  • Support senior researchers on exploratory analysis across Bitcoin, EVM ecosystems, and major non-EVM blockchains.
  • Query and analyze blockchain datasets using SQL and APIs, including our internal data platforms, to validate hypotheses quickly.
  • Use modern analytical and AI-assisted tooling to speed up attribution, summarization, and ad hoc research.
  • Collaborate with engineering on datasets, monitoring systems, and research tooling.

Requirements

Must Haves

Experience & Knowledge

  • 2 to 3 years of experience in blockchain analysis, crypto research, or a related field.
  • Demonstrable, hands-on experience with on-chain attribution: wallet clustering, entity analysis, and investigating unknown addresses.
  • Publicly available research or analysis that we can review before interviews (for example, threads, reports, dashboards, or write-ups).
  • Working familiarity with Bitcoin, EVM ecosystems, and at least one major non-EVM blockchain.
  • Understanding of how on-chain activity such as exchange flows, unlocks, and treasury movements relates to market behavior.

Technical & Analytical Skills

  • Working proficiency in SQL and APIs, with experience querying large blockchain datasets.
  • Experience with blockchain analytics and visualization platforms such as Dune, Flipside, Arkham, Nansen, Etherscan, Solscan, or similar tools.
  • Familiarity with Bitcoin's UTXO model and associated transaction analysis techniques.
  • Python or a similar language for research and prototyping.
  • Good judgment about what is signal and what is noise in incomplete or fast-moving data.

Operational & Communication Skills

  • Strong attention to detail while tracking several assets and themes at once.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, especially under time pressure.
  • Ownership, self-direction, and intellectual curiosity.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across research, trading, and engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience at a trading firm, hedge fund, market intelligence firm, or crypto-native research organization.
  • Experience building monitoring dashboards, alerts, or information aggregation workflows.
  • Experience interpreting real-time market events, such as unlocks, governance actions, liquidations, hacks, and bridge movements.
  • Familiarity with derivatives positioning or cross-venue flows.
  • A network within the crypto ecosystem and familiarity with key entities, protocols, and information channels.

Interview Process

  1. CV Screening – We will review your application based on the qualifications and experience outlined above.
  2. Phone Interview – A discussion with the Talent Acquisition Partner to better understand your background, career motivations, and overall alignment.
  3. Written follow-up – A few short written questions on your on-chain research process, reviewed by the research team.
  4. First Interview – Interview with our On-chain Research Lead on your experience and general technical knowledge.
  5. Second Interview – A deeper look at your attribution methodology, how you validate on-chain signals, and your public research.
  6. CIO Interview – A concluding discussion to evaluate cultural fit, strategic alignment, and how you resonate with the firm's values.

Company Values

Throughout the process, you'll be assessed for cultural fit through our company values:

  • Drive – We believe the best team members are deeply passionate about what they do. That passion fuels their growth, drives them to seek out the best teams, and leads them to hold high expectations of themselves in pursuit of excellence.
  • Ownership – We aim to extend ownership as broadly as possible across the firm. In return, we value people who take initiative, step up when needed, and treat the company’s goals as their own.
  • Judgment – We value those who see the big picture and focus on what truly drives impact and results. They use time wisely, adapt across domains, and always prioritize outcomes over comfort zones.
  • Openness – We foster a culture of open communication, mutual challenge, and shared growth. We believe constructive debate and proactive knowledge sharing lead us closer to the truth—and better decisions.
  • Competence – We work with people who bring exceptional intellectual strength. What sets them apart isn’t just what they know—it’s how they use what they know to navigate change, adapt quickly, and contribute meaningfully in fast-changing environments.
  • Resilience – We perform under pressure. Markets move fast, and so do we—but we stay grounded, focused, and calm. We embrace uncertainty, learn from setbacks, and adapt quickly without losing sight of long-term goals.

jobs.description:
Director, AP Japanese Language and Culture, Curriculum and Assessment

College Board – AP & I

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type:This is a full-time position


About the Team

The AP Curriculum and Assessment Team at College Board (125+ staff) collaborates with colleagues across all aspects of the AP Program to develop, manage, and deliver AP’s 43 courses in a wide variety of subject areas. AP® is a rigorous academic program built on the commitment, passion, and hard work of students and educators from secondary schools and higher education. AP provides willing and academically prepared high school students with the opportunity to study and learn at the college level. AP’s course teams comprised of educators and disciplinary experts ensure that course curricula are aligned to higher education expectations and reflect the state of the art in the discipline, contribute to instructional resources and tools for teachers, and develop assessments that allow students in these courses to demonstrate their mastery of course content and skills. AP leads in strategic use of AI to expand student access, strengthen instructional design and professional support, and enhance assessment creation and exam analysis. The English, World Languages, and Arts department, which includes English Literature, English Language, Spanish Language, Japanese Language, French Language, German Language, Japanese Language, Japanese Language, Latin, Music Theory, Spanish Literature, and Art and Design is currently comprised of approximately 35 people supporting 14 courses in the AP portfolio. 


About the Opportunity

As the Director I, AP Japanese Language and Culture you will be responsible for preserving and improving the quality and validity of the AP Program’s core deliverables within the subject domain: the exam, the course curriculum, and the professional development content. You are also responsible for item development and management from authoring to administration; training and collaborating with subject-matter experts (SMEs), typically college professors and secondary school teachers. You will ethically and effectively integrate AI technologies in assessment creation and review. This includes judiciously using AI assisted tools to support fairness, validity, and innovation in AP assessments. You will train SMEs on assessment development protocols, translate between academics and technical experts (psychometricians), and collaborate to develop formative assessment materials and resources to support AP Japanese Language and Culture teachers worldwide. You will serve as a point of contact in AP for committees and communities of subject-matter experts and will be responsible for the curriculum and assessment for AP Japanese Language and Culture, and, in partnership with other AP teams, further the strategic growth of AP Japanese Language and Culture across the globe. Additionally, you may have the opportunity to present, speak, and moderate dialogue with academic and membership audiences to ensure that ongoing change and improvement within AP courses and exams is understood, accepted, and supported in secondary and post-secondary educational communities.  


In this role, you will:


Assessment Development and Scoring (45-75%)  

  • Serve as an assessment leader for AP Japanese Language and Culture, with primary responsibility for assessment development for AP Japanese Language and Culture. Your work in developing and revising test content is of the quality that requires only minimal adjustments based on feedback from your manager and other program leaders. 
  • Independently lead processes for authoring and revising assessment content, including training educator constituents and leveraging generative AI to author and/or review assessment content, improving and/or making more efficient assessment processes and outputs.
  • Independently lead the development and management of assessment content (formative and summative) and scoring materials for AP Japanese Language and Culture through iterative review stages with multiple internal and external stakeholders, including the AP Japanese Language and Culture Team, Assessment Production team, Test Development Committee, and the Chief Reader, as appropriate.
  • Independently lead the development of assessment forms for AP Japanese Language and Culture, ensuring the AP Exam development aligns with approved curricula and test specifications.
  • Lead multiple face-to-face, weekend meetings, and virtual meetings (during work week, evenings, or weekends) annually with the AP Japanese Language and Culture Test Development Committee. You strategize and develop an agenda and approach to ensure the committee’s meeting time is of the highest productivity; you successfully adapt and pivot during the meeting as needed; and you successfully resolve all post-meeting item content edits.
  • Train and directly supervise Test Development Committee members in AP Japanese Language and Culture as content development contributors and reviewers. Recruit educators for the AP Japanese Language and Culture Development Committee and other opportunities to support AP Program.
  • Lead the successful scoring of student responses for AP Japanese Language and Culture Exams at the annual scoring event in person and online—the “AP Reading”—and produce AP Reading publications materials for teacher and student use. You plan all year, with increasing intensity in the months leading up to the Reading, ensuring all workflow steps for this incredibly complex event, as well as all post-Reading activities, are accounted for and successfully executed. 

Assessment Quality and Process (10-15%) 

  • Contribute to current research and best practices in assessment, and engage regularly with AP Curriculum & Assessment colleagues to align on standards and shared principles guiding AP’s assessment directions 
  • Support assessment workstreams within the AP English, World Languages, and Arts Department. 
  • Contribute to processes for efficient, high-quality assessment development. 
  • Contribute to initiatives to refine and improve question task models as well as exam design in collaboration with AP Curriculum & Assessment leaders and aligned to other College Board initiatives to achieve psychometric and disciplinary best practices on AP Japanese Language and Culture exams. 
  • Monitor exam validity, security, reliability, fairness, and quality, as well as reader reliability in accordance with established Program thresholds for AP Japanese Language and Culture exam, identifying areas for improvement and executing on targeted improvement initiatives. 
  • Collaborate with psychometrics and AP Curriculum & Assessment staff to establish fair, reliable, and valid cut scores for AP Japanese Language and Culture exam. 

 

Course Development, Program Support, and Stakeholder Engagement (5-25%) 

  • Refine and improve AP Japanese Language and Culture Framework to ensure clear and explicit learning outcomes that align with strategic priorities, including ensuring college/disciplinary standards as well as expanding the scope of reaching a broader audience of AP students.  
  • Collaborate with AP teams to support the development of new products for AP Japanese Language and Culture designed to address unmet teacher instructional needs, potentially including developing prototypes, participating in small-scale market-testing, and creating models for subsequent development in conjunction with other AP workstreams. 
  • Recruit educators for the AP Japanese Language and Culture Development Committee and other opportunities to support AP Program. 
  • Serve as a recognized and trusted resource within the educator community by collaboration and engagement with the community to drive teacher satisfaction with AP Japanese Language and Culture and its exam. 
  • Collaborate with the AP Professional learning team to support AP Japanese Language and Culture consultants and teachers. 
  • Work with the AP Higher Education team to co-develop and implement plans to raise college and university awareness of AP Japanese Language and Culture courses and exams, including recruiting college faculty to participate in the AP Reading, co-leading the planning and execution of discipline-specific AP Faculty Colloquia events, and supporting Visiting and Virtual Fellows Programs.  

About You

To qualify for this role, you must have:

  • A Master’s degree in Japanese Language or a directly related discipline, and knowledge of current trends in the discipline (required), although a doctorate in the discipline is strongly preferred  
  • Native to near-native fluency in Japanese.
  • Expertise in Japanese Language with at least 5 years of experience in standardized assessment development or related work; experience with digital assessment and teaching preferred 
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with solid technical proficiency and a customer-focused mindset 
  • Excellent organizational and planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and maintain close attention to detail, including proofreading 
  • Demonstrated ability to implement processes and procedures, manage project plans and schedules, and maintain tracking documentation 
  • Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across all levels, and engage in giving and receiving constructive feedback 
  • Ability to travel 6-8 times per year, plus up to two additional weeks for the AP Reading; must be eligible to work in the United States 

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.


A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $96,000 - $135,000
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.
