jobs.description:
Description

Position: Credit Analyst / Para-Broker (End-to-End Loan Processor)

Salary: Php 80,000 - 160,000 (Salary will be based depending on the candidate's experience)

Working Hours & Conditions: Full Time (Independent Contractor Arrangement) , Will follow Queensland business hours

Holidays:TBC

ABOUT THE COMPANY:

The client is a mortgage brokerage company that has been operating since 2010. With a background in complex self employed and investor lending and structure, they focus now on individual, tailored solutions to help people buy their dream home. They take time with clients to uncover solutions, educate, and provide long term support. The client does currently does all of the credit analysis and processing himself and wants to step back from it so he can focus on clients, marketing, referrals and growing the business. The role exists to support the broker and clients by lifting productivity and releasing the broker's time to bring in more business.

Role Overview

This is an end-to-end credit analyst and loan processor, a hybrid of credit analyst and para-broker. It is a senior role: the person takes a file from first document through to settlement, working out the client's position and the best strategy, preparing lending proposals, packaging and lodging applications, and keeping clients updated. They should be able to own the work, give advice on how to structure it, and run it without close direction. This role will be the template for the future team, and it will be replicated over time to build redundancy.

Key Responsibilities

Pre-Credit Assessment

  • Collect, check and file supporting documents in Google Drive using the company naming format
  • Verify and update the Mercury Fact Find from supporting documents, and update Mercury and BrokerEngine with client details
  • Download and examine Equifax reports through Mercury, and examine the MLE
  • Verify property estimates using RPData, and order AVMs where equity is critical
  • Request missing, outstanding or extra documents needed to complete the assessment

Credit Research & Strategy

  • Complete Quickli servicing from the Fact Find and documents, and complete the Funding Position and Preliminary Assessment in BrokerEngine
  • Identify information to confirm, actions the client must take, policies to review and key strategies to improve the client's position
  • Assess current and future ability to reach the client's goal, and record capacity, limitations, options and the recommended strategy

Lending Proposals

  • Complete the Research form, list policy hurdles and potential lenders, confirm policies with lenders and shortlist
  • Run pricing requests and escalations, and order valuations and update security details
  • Complete the Product Comparison, Funding Position and Mudmap, and select lenders based on policy, servicing and cost
  • Create the Loan Strategy Proposal document and save everything to the client file

Loan Processing & Submission

  • Complete broker notes and generate the PDF for submission, prepare Mercury and compliance documents, and finalise Mercury for lodgement
  • Prepare AOL (and LoanApp), review and approve documents, and ensure accuracy before submitting
  • Get application and compliance forms signed, collect outstanding documents and submit to the lender

Approvals, AIPs, Construction & Settlement

  • Review approval conditions against funding positions, update key dates and the document portal, and update solicitors on formal approval
  • Convert AIPs to formal approvals, ordering valuations and updating the funding position
  • Handle construction loans: cost analysis, insurance, warranty, contracts, council-approved plans, progress payments and building insurance at handover
  • After approval, check the loan agreement against the approved product, send signing instructions and disbursement details, and record loan and offset details
  • At settlement, generate the settlement advice, email the client from the template, update records, archive the file and prepare the review

Client Communication & Daily Responsibilities

  • Keep clients updated using the BrokerEngine email and SMS templates: every 2 days at initial assessment, daily at signing and from lodgement to approval, and immediately on status changes
  • Complete Preliminary Assessments (Your Home Plans) and Loan Strategy Proposals as they are ready, and action MIRs within one business day
  • Clarify credit questions with the broker when required, and keep the BrokerEngine checklist up to date
  • Manage individual and shared inboxes, action items within one business day, and chase clients for outstanding information
  • Build and maintain the company's process guides, working with the broker

What Success Looks Like

  • Manages 5 to 7 client lodgements t settlements a month, and processes an additional 5 Your Home Plans a month
  • Frees the broker for client conversations, marketing and lead generation, client reviews and workshopping with clients
  • Keeps the business running smoothly when the broker is away or focused elsewhere
  • Leaves time to explore productivity improvements as the team grows

Requirements

Non-negotiable

  • 3 to 5+ years' experience as a credit analyst or para-broker in an Australian mortgage brokerage
  • Strong complex reasoning and problem-solving skills, able to spot client limitations and build solutions
  • Experience with complex loan structuring, and with PAYG and basic self-employed lending, including reading self-employed financials
  • Extensive experience with Quickli and lender calculators
  • Experience running pricing approvals and valuations, packaging files in Mercury and lodging in both AOL and LoanApp
  • Managing submissions through to approval and settlement, with a strong understanding of mortgage broking compliance (NCCP and best interests)
  • Strong organisation and self-management, and decisiveness
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • Available for Queensland business hours

Strong Plus

  • BrokerEngine experience (preferred, not essential), and 3+ years across Mercury and BrokerEngine
  • Complex self-employed lending and policy solutions, and structuring for residential property investors
  • Using competitor pricing to win better offers, and SMSF lending
  • Experience with valuation tools and construction loans

Working Style

The ideal person is self-motivated and takes pride in what they deliver, and wants a long-term career that challenges and rewards them.

  • Takes ownership of decisions, works independently and doesn't depend on direction
  • Extremely accurate and organised, and thrives in systems and processes
  • Task-focused, fulfilled by completing work well
  • A strong problem-solver who sees the big picture of lending
  • Kind and empathetic with customers, and unfazed by customer stress
  • Confident in their abilities, communicating well with the team and customers

Benefits

  • Work from home setup
  • Morning Shift Role
  • Independent Contractor Arrangement

jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.title: UX Researcher
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a UX Researcher to help Bask Health better understand how users interact with our software and identify opportunities to improve usability across the platform.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform connects merchant tools, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce capabilities.

As a UX Researcher, you'll study how people navigate these experiences, complete tasks, interpret information, and respond to different interface designs. Your findings will help product teams make informed decisions about how the platform should work.

This is a hands-on research role focused on evaluating digital experiences through user interviews, usability testing, observational studies, and other research methods. You'll help teams understand where users encounter friction, which interactions are confusing, and how proposed changes affect the overall experience.

Your work will span merchant-facing and patient-facing software. You may evaluate merchant onboarding, dashboard navigation, storefront configuration, patient questionnaires, checkout experiences, account settings, or other complex workflows.

You'll work closely with product designers to test prototypes, evaluate interaction patterns, and identify opportunities to simplify interfaces before development.

You'll also collaborate with content designers and UX writers to understand how users interpret labels, instructions, error messages, and other interface content.

You'll partner with product managers to define research questions, prioritize usability concerns, and ensure studies address important product decisions.

You'll work with engineers to understand technical constraints and help evaluate how implemented experiences compare with intended designs.

You'll conduct moderated and unmoderated usability studies, user interviews, concept evaluations, and task-based assessments. You'll select appropriate methods based on the questions being investigated and the stage of product development.

You'll also analyze research findings, identify recurring patterns, and communicate recommendations that help teams make practical improvements.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll need to conduct research with appropriate attention to participant privacy, consent, sensitive information, and approved clinical workflow boundaries.

You'll help maintain organized research documentation and contribute to repeatable research practices that make usability insights accessible across the company.

We're looking for someone who is curious about how people use software, comfortable investigating complex workflows, and able to turn user observations into clear recommendations that improve product experiences.

What You'll Do

  • Conduct UX research across Bask Health's merchant-facing and patient-facing software experiences.
  • Plan and execute usability studies for existing and proposed product features.
  • Conduct moderated user interviews to understand behaviors and usability challenges.
  • Support unmoderated usability testing and structured task evaluations.
  • Develop research plans, study objectives, and participant criteria.
  • Create usability tasks, interview guides, and research discussion materials.
  • Evaluate navigation, information architecture, and interaction patterns.
  • Test prototypes to identify usability problems before development.
  • Research how users complete multi-step onboarding and configuration workflows.
  • Evaluate merchant dashboards, settings pages, and administrative interfaces.
  • Study patient questionnaires, forms, and checkout experiences.
  • Identify confusing instructions, labels, and interface terminology.
  • Collaborate with content designers to evaluate comprehension and clarity.
  • Work with product designers to validate proposed interaction patterns.
  • Partner with product managers to prioritize usability research opportunities.
  • Recruit and screen research participants through approved processes.
  • Observe user behavior and identify recurring friction points.
  • Analyze qualitative research findings to identify patterns and themes.
  • Incorporate available behavioral data and usability metrics where appropriate.
  • Evaluate task completion, user errors, and workflow efficiency.
  • Develop research summaries and actionable design recommendations.
  • Present usability findings to product, design, and engineering teams.
  • Support iterative testing throughout product development.
  • Conduct post-launch usability evaluations when needed.
  • Help establish reusable usability testing templates and research practices.
  • Maintain organized research documentation and findings.
  • Follow appropriate participant consent, privacy, and data-handling procedures.
  • Independently manage assigned UX research projects from planning through synthesis and presentation.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional experience in UX research, user research, human-computer interaction, or a closely related field.
  • Portfolio or case studies demonstrating UX research methods and findings.
  • Experience planning and conducting usability studies for digital products.
  • Strong understanding of qualitative research methods.
  • Experience conducting moderated user interviews.
  • Familiarity with unmoderated usability testing.
  • Ability to develop clear research questions and study objectives.
  • Experience creating usability tasks and research discussion guides.
  • Understanding of user-centered design principles.
  • Ability to evaluate navigation, interaction patterns, and complex workflows.
  • Experience identifying usability problems and recommending improvements.
  • Familiarity with usability metrics and task-based evaluation.
  • Experience synthesizing qualitative findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Ability to communicate research results to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Experience collaborating closely with product designers and product managers.
  • Familiarity with wireframes, prototypes, and iterative product design.
  • Experience evaluating digital interfaces across different stages of development.
  • Understanding of research ethics and participant consent.
  • Familiarity with participant recruitment and screening.
  • Experience organizing and documenting research findings.
  • Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to balance research rigor with practical development timelines.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple studies.
  • Ability to independently deliver high-quality UX research work.

Nice to Have

  • Experience researching SaaS platforms or business software.
  • Familiarity with merchant-facing dashboards and administrative applications.
  • Experience evaluating e-commerce or direct-to-consumer product experiences.
  • Background in healthcare, telehealth, or patient-facing digital software.
  • Experience testing patient onboarding or intake questionnaires.
  • Familiarity with complex forms and multi-step workflows.
  • Understanding of healthcare-related privacy considerations.
  • Experience conducting research involving sensitive information.
  • Familiarity with tools such as UserTesting, Maze, Dovetail, Lookback, or comparable research platforms.
  • Experience evaluating Figma prototypes.
  • Understanding of quantitative usability measures.
  • Experience combining usability findings with product analytics.
  • Familiarity with accessibility research and inclusive testing practices.
  • Experience conducting remote usability studies.
  • Understanding of information architecture testing methods.
  • Experience with first-click testing, tree testing, or card sorting.
  • Familiarity with white-label or multi-tenant SaaS products.
  • Experience researching AI-assisted interfaces.
  • Understanding of research operations and insight repositories.
  • Experience working in fast-moving, cross-functional product teams.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI Platform
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Software Engineer, AI Platform to build and maintain the foundational software infrastructure that supports AI-powered applications across Bask Health.

As Bask expands its use of artificial intelligence across merchant tools, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and internal systems, we need reliable shared services that allow engineering teams to develop and deploy AI capabilities efficiently.

This role focuses on the platform infrastructure behind those applications. You'll build reusable APIs, model integration services, inference gateways, data access components, and operational tools that make it easier for other engineers to incorporate AI into production software.

You'll work with backend technologies, cloud infrastructure, databases, model providers, and distributed systems to develop scalable services that handle AI requests, manage application resources, and support reliable execution.

Your work may include centralized model access, request routing, usage tracking, authentication, rate limiting, prompt configuration, observability, and infrastructure that supports retrieval and agent-based applications.

You'll collaborate with applied AI engineers, machine learning engineers, product engineers, and infrastructure specialists to understand their technical requirements and develop platform capabilities that can be reused across multiple products.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll also help ensure AI infrastructure respects privacy requirements, tenant isolation, access controls, and approved data-handling practices. You'll design systems that allow teams to innovate without compromising security or reliability.

This is a hands-on engineering role with ownership over production infrastructure and shared developer capabilities. You'll write code, improve system architecture, investigate operational issues, and help establish engineering patterns that support Bask's growing AI capabilities.

We're looking for an engineer who enjoys building reliable backend systems, thinks carefully about scalability and developer experience, and understands how strong infrastructure enables teams to ship better products.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and maintain shared infrastructure for AI-powered applications across Bask Health.
  • Develop backend services and APIs that support model integration and AI application execution.
  • Build reusable components that allow engineering teams to access large language models consistently.
  • Develop centralized model integration services and inference request handling.
  • Implement routing and configuration capabilities for multiple model providers.
  • Build systems for managing model API credentials, authentication, and access permissions.
  • Develop request validation, structured output handling, and standardized error responses.
  • Implement rate limiting, retries, timeouts, and fallback mechanisms for model API requests.
  • Build usage tracking and cost monitoring for AI services.
  • Develop infrastructure that supports prompt configuration, versioning, and controlled updates.
  • Create shared services for embeddings, retrieval, and knowledge-grounded AI applications.
  • Build APIs and integration patterns that support AI agents and workflow automation.
  • Develop secure data access components for AI applications.
  • Ensure AI services respect tenant boundaries and application authorization requirements.
  • Build observability systems for model requests, latency, errors, and operational performance.
  • Implement structured logging and distributed tracing across AI services.
  • Develop automated testing and deployment pipelines for AI platform components.
  • Improve infrastructure reliability, fault tolerance, and service availability.
  • Optimize backend performance, throughput, and infrastructure costs.
  • Design scalable asynchronous processing and background job systems.
  • Integrate AI platform services with existing application databases and backend infrastructure.
  • Build internal developer tools and documentation that simplify AI application development.
  • Collaborate with applied AI engineers to identify common infrastructure needs.
  • Support machine learning engineers with reliable model-serving and evaluation integrations.
  • Investigate production incidents and resolve infrastructure-related failures.
  • Participate in architecture discussions, technical planning, and code reviews.
  • Establish reusable engineering patterns for secure and maintainable AI integrations.
  • Own assigned platform services from technical design through deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, preferably in backend, platform, or infrastructure engineering.
  • Demonstrated experience building and maintaining production backend services.
  • Strong programming skills in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or comparable backend languages.
  • Experience designing and developing APIs and service integrations.
  • Strong understanding of backend application architecture and distributed systems fundamentals.
  • Familiarity with large language models and modern AI application integration patterns.
  • Experience integrating third-party APIs or external services into production applications.
  • Understanding of authentication, authorization, and secure service communication.
  • Experience working with relational databases and application data models.
  • Familiarity with asynchronous processing, background jobs, and event-driven systems.
  • Experience designing systems that handle errors, retries, timeouts, and service failures.
  • Understanding of cloud infrastructure and production deployment practices.
  • Familiarity with automated testing and continuous integration workflows.
  • Experience working with logging, monitoring, and production observability tools.
  • Understanding of system performance, latency, scalability, and reliability.
  • Experience designing reusable software components and shared engineering services.
  • Familiarity with API versioning, configuration management, and service maintenance.
  • Understanding of data privacy and secure application development.
  • Experience using Git, code review, and collaborative software development practices.
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex backend and infrastructure issues.
  • Experience writing maintainable, well-documented production code.
  • Ability to evaluate engineering tradeoffs involving performance, complexity, and operational costs.
  • Experience collaborating with engineers across multiple product or technical teams.
  • Strong technical problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Ability to independently own engineering projects from design through deployment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building infrastructure for AI or machine learning applications.
  • Familiarity with OpenAI, Anthropic, or comparable model APIs.
  • Experience building model gateways, inference proxies, or centralized AI integration services.
  • Familiarity with multi-model routing and provider fallback strategies.
  • Experience with TypeScript and Node.js backend development.
  • Familiarity with tRPC, Prisma, Drizzle, or similar application development tools.
  • Experience working with AWS Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, or comparable cloud services.
  • Familiarity with serverless infrastructure and infrastructure-as-code tools.
  • Experience with SST or similar application deployment frameworks.
  • Familiarity with containerization and distributed service deployment.
  • Experience building systems for API rate limiting, usage metering, or cost allocation.
  • Familiarity with embeddings, vector databases, and retrieval infrastructure.
  • Experience supporting retrieval-augmented generation applications.

jobs.description:
About the company

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. This is a task-based, independent contractor opportunity, not an employment relationship. Participation is limited to this project.

Project Highlights

  • Earnings per approved task: a fixed rate for each task, set in advance
  • Fully self-scheduled: no minimum hours and no set schedule; you choose which tasks to take and when
  • Remote: open to US-licensed physicians based in eligible US states
  • No patient contact, no malpractice exposure: you review written clinical cases
  • All contributors are license-verified physicians
  • $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved

What this project involves

We're looking for physicians (MD/DO) with an active, unrestricted US medical license to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation project. General and internal medicine are the main focus. Each task is a written clinical case, assessed against the project's acceptance criteria. Contributors may:

  • Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor "trap" answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
  • Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;
  • Check whether the reasoning chain reaches the answer from vignette facts alone, correct reasoning traces, and write short rationales.

Each case receives three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You're improving the AI tools you'll eventually use yourself.

What we look for

This project is a good fit for US-licensed physicians looking for a flexible, time-limited project they can fit around their other commitments. Ideally, contributors will have:

  • Medical degree (MD or DO) and an active, unrestricted US medical license (verified at onboarding and re-checked monthly);
  • Board certification or completed residency training, with direct patient care experience (attending-level preferred). Practising or retired physicians welcome;
  • Broad, multi-system diagnostic and treatment experience (internal, family, emergency, or hospital medicine);
  • Strong clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, next-step management, and application of evidence-based guidelines;
  • Prior experience in medical AI evaluation, clinical content or exam-question review, or medical annotation/QA (a plus);
  • Strong written English (C1+).

This project is not suitable for medical students, unlicensed medical graduates, non-physician clinicians (NPs, PAs, nurses, pharmacists), or non-clinical healthcare titles.

How it works

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join the project → Complete tasks → Get paid for approved tasks

Flexibility

You decide whether, when, and how much to contribute. There are no minimum hours, set schedules, or required availability. Task availability varies with project phases. Tasks are submitted through the platform and are approved when they meet the project’s acceptance criteria.

Earnings

Earnings are paid only for completed and approved tasks. Each task type has a fixed rate. There is no time tracking and no hour logging. There are no tiers or speed adjustments to the rate. QA and adjudication tasks have a higher per-task rate.

  • $50 one-time onboarding reward, paid once your first task on the project is approved.
  • Quality incentives: additional earnings for high-quality approved tasks, on terms set out in the project guidelines.

jobs.title: Academic Curriculum and Content Development Manager
jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

Academic Curriculum and Content Development Manager
Remote (India) | Full-time
Also searched as: Content Development Manager, Academic Content Manager, Curriculum Manager, Curriculum Team Lead, International Curriculum Manager, Content Manager (IB / IGCSE / A-Level)
Could you run Contour's India content team across every subject, holding its work to an Australian exam standard without needing to be the expert in each one?
On a typical day you might catch a QA flag on a question set before it ships in the morning, review an AI step that drafts question variants with your Curriculum Designer after lunch, and close the afternoon agreeing with an academic owner in Melbourne what a study-design change means for next week's content.
About Contour
We operate across three brands. The India team, which falls under the Global Enablement and Support pillar, is the global capability centre (GCC) Contour is building: it runs delivery, automation, people, and operations for the whole organisation.
The Kind of People Who Thrive Here
Contour started in 2020 as one classroom in a university library. In 2022 three full-time team members ran the business on. Today we are about 600 people across Australia and India, and much of what we run was built by someone who noticed it was missing.
The work matters. More than 10,000 students rely on what we build, from the booklets they study from to the systems their families pay through. The people who do well here care about that and want to know their work made a difference to those students.
They own their work end to end, start things without being asked, and finish what they commit to. They tell the truth early, including when something is off and what they have already tried, and write decisions down so the next person can pick them up. They give direct feedback and ask for it back.
The pace is fast. Small problems are fixed the same week, bigger ones within the six-week cycle, and whoever spots the problem usually gets to lead the fix. We keep refining how we work, and you are expected to improve the processes you own.
We hire on what you have built and run yourself, and growth works the same way. Time with us counts, but scope, title and pay move with what you deliver and how much you raise the bar on what you own.
The GCC is being built now, seat by seat. This one decides how well Contour's content holds up as it grows.
About This Role
You lead Contour's India content team: the curriculum designers, content developers, question writers and markers who build what students learn from, across the Victorian (VCE), Queensland (QCE) and, from 2027, New South Wales (HSC) curricula.
Your team's work is set and signed off in Australia. The academic owners, Heads of Subject and curriculum leads, set the standard for each subject and approve what ships, and onshore curriculum leads write content too, so yours has to fit alongside theirs. The Production lead is your peer: their team designs, formats and publishes finished assets from what yours writes. Everything else is yours: the people, the workflow, and the systems that get each item there.
This is international work. Contour's students sit Australian exams, their study designs are set by Australian authorities, and the people who judge your team's output are Australian teachers and students. You need to have built content for a curriculum outside India and worked closely with academic owners in another country, so you know how an overseas exam board thinks about rigour, wording and marking.
Two things separate a strong hire here from a competent one. First, you run quality as a system. You are not expected to be an expert in every curriculum: you turn what the academic owners mean by good into checks and measures that get every specialist there consistently, so drafts don't need rewriting at the end. Second, you protect quality at speed. With a turnaround of under a week, when something is at risk you make the call early on the information you have.
We are looking for someone tech-forward. Contour runs on tools, and the India team has its own automation and Internal Product teams to build with. The strongest candidates have already used AI and automation to make a content team do more with the same people: AI drafting first versions and question variants, automated checks catching errors before a reviewer sees them, and items tagged and tracked without manual effort. You spot where a tool can take work off the team, set it up with the people who use it, and make sure quality holds.
You build on the content team already in place: Curriculum Designers, Content Developers, and the Question Writers and Markers, who write practice items and grade learners' work, all report to you. We want a player-coach who leads by example. You have enough hands-on curriculum and content experience to coach your leads and specialists, judge quality, challenge estimates and step in when needed; subject specialists hold deep expertise in their subjects. The seat may later take in UCAT (the medical-school entry test) and selective-entry school exams. Contour is scaling and hires for the long term: the scope of this seat grows with the platform, and what you deliver decides how fast.
Much of what Contour students study from passes through this team, so a gap that slips past review reaches a learner. Get the system right, and each new subject or exam builds on it.
​
What You Will Do
  • Turn the academic bar into a working system:Establish what good looks like subject by subject, against each study design, then build the checklists, KPIs and review points that keep output there.
  • Run the create-and-QA cycle:Track output on a dashboard you build, so no discipline falls behind the teaching calendar, and step in ahead of any slip.
  • Keep up with study-design changes:When VCAA, QCAA or NESA update a study design or exam format, map what changes, plan the rework and land it before the term that needs it.
  • Mark on schedule:Return marked assignments within the turnaround promised to learners, and run calibration sessions so feedback reads the same whoever marked it.
  • Keep the academic owners close:When their expectations change, agree what that means before writing starts, and brief the whole group the same week, across the India–Australia time difference.
  • Supercharge the team with AI and automation:AI-drafted question variants, automated answer and formatting checks, tagging every item to its syllabus point, with tracking in Notion or Monday, and keep finding the next manual step to remove. Specialists keep the final call on every item.
  • Coach directly:Run structured 1:1s and performance conversations with every designer, developer, writer and marker, and make sure everyone knows why their work matters.
  • Decide how the function grows:When Contour adds a subject, a format or volume, choose which lever to pull, hire where the answer is headcount, and prepare what it needs in advance.
  • Fix the cycle where it breaks:Find where creation or checking loses time or lets errors through, including errors found after release, and fix the cause in the process rather than in one draft.
  • Report what is shipping:Keep throughput, pass rates and rework visible, so the VP of Global Enablement and Support and the academic owners can see where content stands without asking.
If a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.

Requirements

What You Need
We weigh what you have built and run more than the years on your CV. You should be able to point to:
  • International exposure (essential):content you built or led for a curriculum outside India, such as Australian (VCE, QCE, HSC), IB, Cambridge IGCSE or A-levels, AP or SAT, and regular work with academic owners, clients or examiners in another country.
  • Tech-forward, AI-first habits (essential):a content or QA step you moved onto AI or automation, such as drafting, checking, tagging or tracking, and what it did for the team's speed and quality.
  • A content or curriculum department you led, spanning subjects beyond your specialism and held to a bar someone else set.
  • A production schedule you ran from brief to release, where deadlines held without corners cut.
  • A tracker that made a standard visible: a checklist, a KPI, a dashboard or a review step others still use.
  • A content function you grew into a new syllabus, a new format or a larger group, and what you put in place first.
  • Performance conversations you led, including one that changed how someone worked.
  • Writers who stepped up to bigger roles under you, and how you helped them.
  • Hands-on experience in academic content, content development or publishing before you managed it, so you know how a question set or unit actually gets made.
  • Excellent written English and clear, confident communication with academic owners in Australia.
If you have delivered these, or can show us how you would here, apply. If you enjoy hands-on work, this seat will suit you; if your recent years have mostly been signing off other people's work, it may feel small.

Nice to Have

  • Australian curriculum experience (VCE, QCE or HSC) in particular.
  • EdTech or education services background.
  • Curriculum design, instructional design or assessment design experience.
  • Experience with automation tools (Zapier, Make, n8n or Apps Script), or building custom GPTs or AI workflows for a team.
What Good Looks Like
  • The cycle holds:output stays on schedule at any volume, with QA never squeezed.
  • Gaps caught early:QA finds the problem before it reaches final sign-off.
  • Marking that agrees:two markers give the same piece of work the same grade and similar feedback.
  • Changes land on time:a study-design update is reflected in Contour's content before the term that needs it.
  • A team that does more with AI:the share of drafting, checking and tagging handled by AI and automation rises each term, with quality held.

Benefits

Fully remote, anywhere in India, and comfortable working across the India and Australia time difference. Compensation is competitive and benchmarked to the role and your experience; we discuss it openly early in the process.
Ready to run the content Contour's students learn from? Apply.

Using a broad understanding of customer engagement strategies, clinical procedures and company facilities, this position provides accurate and timely information to create an experience that is easy, empathetic and differentiated in the marketplace.

7. Where applicable, collects pre-payments and verifies insurance coverage to ensure “no surprises” and enable patient ease.

8. Services inbound and outbound customer and staff communications for all facilities in the states in which they operate. Works with various departments and staff to provide accurate managed care information.

Requires skills and abilities typically attained with minimum of 1 or more years of customer service or related experience in a healthcare setting, such as medical office/clinic or hospital scheduling. Other acceptable experience includes lab, medical transcription, medical assistant or receptionist in a medical setting or other equivalent experience. Demonstrated ability to provide essential customer service and knowledge in a high paced inbound contact center environment Ability to use technology tools to research and obtain accurate information to respond to customer inquiries via incoming calls, emails and/or instant messaging/chat avenues while maintaining a professional solutions and service-oriented demeanor at all times. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to maintain a positive and helpful attitude with customers, providers and clinic operations. jobs.title: AI Evaluation Engineer — Agentic Systems (H/F)
jobs.description:
Dans le cadre de notre croissance et afin de renforcer notre Squad AI Quality & Evaluation, nous recherchons un.e AI Evaluation Engineer — Agentic Systems.

Intégré.e au sein de nos équipes, en télétravail avec une flexibilité sur la région parisienne, vous interviendrez sur l'un des métiers les plus stratégiques de l'IA : garantir, mesurer et fiabiliser le comportement des agents et systèmes multi-agents avant leur mise en production. Un domaine qui s'invente aujourd'hui, où vous mettrez en pratique vos acquis en QA et développerez de nouvelles compétences à la frontière de l'IA.

MISSIONS:

=> Concevoir des stratégies d'évaluation pour agents et systèmes multi-agents : trajectoires, orchestration d'outils (tool use), raisonnement multi-étapes, gestion de mémoire et de contexte
=> Évaluer au-delà du résultat final : détecter les échecs intermédiaires, la propagation d'erreurs et les dérives de comportement le long de la trajectoire
=> Concevoir et éprouver des workflows agentiques : décomposition de tâches, enchaînement d'agents (planner / executor / critic), points de contrôle et garde-fous
=> Construire des jeux de tests et scénarios de simulation d'utilisateurs : personas, cas limites, tests adversariaux
=> Exploiter le prompt engineering comme levier d'évaluation : prompts de test, LLM-as-a-judge, rubriques d'évaluation
=> Industrialiser l'évaluation dans les pipelines CI/CD : évaluation automatisée, détection de régressions, quality gates avant déploiement
=> Définir les métriques qui comptent pour un agent : réussite de tâche, fidélité, robustesse, sécurité, coût, latence, consommation de tokens
=> Combiner évaluation automatisée et évaluation humaine (human-in-the-loop), et arbitrer entre les deux
=> Documenter et diffuser les bonnes pratiques d'évaluation agentique auprès des équipes

PROFIL:

=> Idéalement une première expérience en évaluation de systèmes IA — en poste, en freelance ou même sur un projet personnel sérieux : ce métier s'invente, nous valorisons ce que vous avez déjà exploré par vous-même

=> Compréhension de ce qui rend l'évaluation d'un agent spécifique : non-déterminisme, comportement probabiliste, trajectoires multi-étapes, échecs intermédiaires, absence de vérité unique — on n'évalue pas une sortie, on score une trajectoire (chaque appel d'outil, chaque état intermédiaire devient une surface d'évaluation)

=> Familiarité avec les approches de scoring : graders à base de règles (code-based), LLM-as-a-judge pour l'ouvert, évaluation humaine — et le bon sens de savoir quand combiner les trois

=> Maîtrise réelle d'au moins un framework ou plateforme d'évaluation IA : DeepEval, Ragas, TruLens, Giskard, Maxim AI, Braintrust, Langfuse, Opik ou équivalent

=> Capacité à construire un eval harness et des jeux de tests : cas experts (goldens), minage de traces de production, scénarios adversariaux

=> Bonnes pratiques de prompt engineering appliquées au test et à l'évaluation : conception de rubriques, prompts de test, calibration du juge

=> Maîtrise de Python et de l'automatisation de tests

=> Sensibilité sécurité IA, robustesse et reproductibilité

=> Une connaissance au moins générale du cadre réglementaire IA — EU AI Act(transparence, gestion des risques, littératie IA) et RGPD — et de son impact sur l'évaluation et la mise en production

=> Idéalement certifié.e ISTQB CT-AI (v2.0) et CT-GenAI — à défaut l'une des deux, avec l'envie d'obtenir la seconde

=> Socle solide en QA / test / qualité logicielle, ou en dev/data avec une vraie envie de basculer vers l'IA agentique

=> Anglais professionnel courant

SOFT SKILLS:

=> Passionné.e par les technologies innovantes et le champ de l'IA agentique

=> Rigoureux.se et doté.e d'un fort esprit critique : un tableau de bord tout vert ne vous suffit pas

=> Désireux.se de vous investir dans des projets challengeants et de gagner rapidement en responsabilités

=> Pédagogue, empathique et "Problem Solver" : vous rendez l'évaluation lisible et actionnable pour les équipes

=> Doté.e d'un excellent relationnel, d'un sens prononcé du service et de la qualité

=> Curieux.se et en veille active : un domaine qui évolue chaque semaine, et vous suivez

=> Excellent niveau de français à l'oral et à l'écrit, l'anglais professionnel étant ici indispensable

The DoorDash Architecture and Security team is looking for a Solutions Architect, Business Technology Security with demonstrated experience and knowledge in Workday Security. This role owns the strategy and design of Workday security architecture, and ensures it translates correctly into the custom, in-house tools and dashboards built downstream of it. This is a strategy and design-focused role so success here depends heavily on your ability to gather clear requirements, write them up well, and communicate design decisions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You will interact directly with senior leaders and cross-functional partners across DoorDash to capture requirements and design lasting, secure solutions that hold up across the full ecosystem.

This role will report to the Sr. Manager, Architecture and Security.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Own the strategy and design of Workday’s security architecture — data models, security groups, domains, and business process security — that serves as DoorDash’s security source of truth for the People organization.
  • Translate that architecture into clear requirements and design documentation that our build team can implement, and that downstream custom tools and dashboards can be built against safely.
  • Review new or proposed custom tooling and downstream reporting needs to identify security touchpoints and data access implications before they’re built, advising on the right design approach.
  • Partner with process owners to define data security policies, protocols, and procedures that protect sensitive HR data across Workday and downstream systems.
  • Conduct regular audits and risk assessments across Workday and the tools and reporting layers downstream of it, maintaining a forward-looking security and data classification roadmap.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert on security, data, and reporting capabilities and limitations, communicating trade-offs clearly to both build teams and non-technical business stakeholders.

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

We're looking for the performance marketer who wants to own profitable growth across Google and Microsoft for our Make & Manage Money business, set the plan, and build the campaigns themselves. Our listicles connect people with offers across personal finance, insurance, banking, credit cards, gaming apps, and more, and winning here means understanding how intent, creative, landing pages, offer selection, partner payouts, and lead quality work together. You'll run an eight-figure annual media portfolio with the freedom to put budget wherever it earns, and the trade is that it's yours: you find what's holding growth back, whether it's in the account or not, and you go get it fixed.

Tip: Only apply if you've directly owned and profitably scaled $10M or more a year in paid media for affiliate or consumer lead generation.

Why This Seat

  • Real ownership. You own the portfolio across Google and Microsoft, set the plan, and make the calls. No layers between you and the result.
  • Partners who can move the levers. Yield, account management, and creative work alongside you on payouts, offers, and landing pages, so you're fixing the whole funnel, not just the account.
  • Room to build. Microsoft audience and native inventory, MSN included, is early for us, and budget follows what works.
  • A team that gets better together. We share what works, own what didn't, and turn wins into playbooks the whole paid team uses.
  • An AI-forward stack. Claude is in the daily workflow, with room to automate analysis, concepting, and creative iteration.

What You'll Bring

  • Ownership, Accountability & Strategy. You set the plan, prioritize the tests, and make the call, then bring your manager recommendations, not questions about what to do next.
  • A track record of profitably scaling affiliate or consumer lead gen, with direct ownership of $10M or more in annual media spend.
    • Buying traffic to competitive affiliate listicles, comparison pages, or multi-offer marketplaces.
  • Hands-on depth in Google Ads or Microsoft Ads, and the range to own a portfolio across both. If your strongest experience is in Microsoft Ads, audience buying, or native inventory, we want to hear from you.
    • Scaling across Search, Display, Demand Gen, YouTube, and native placements.
  • A real grasp of affiliate economics: partner payouts, revenue per click, conversion rates, offer mix, traffic quality, ROAS, and margin.
  • A habit of finding the actual constraint. You can tell whether a problem sits in the buying, the creative, the landing page, the offer, the payout, or the measurement, and you go to the team that owns the fix with a clear ask.
  • Clear, direct communication, including short performance updates that say what changed, why it matters, and what you need.

Nice to Have

  • Running across several consumer categories or variable-payout partner programs.
  • Using AI and self-serve creative tools to speed up analysis and asset iteration.
  • Working with competitive intelligence tools and in regulated consumer categories.
  • Building playbooks or mentoring other media buyers.

What You'll Own

  • Strategy and execution across Google Search, Demand Gen, YouTube, and Microsoft audience and native inventory, MSN included.
  • Budget allocation, pacing, forecasting, reporting, and profitability for the portfolio.
  • A prioritized growth plan that names the biggest constraints and the tests most likely to move the business.
  • The case to Sales, Account Management, Yield, Creative, Product, and Analytics for what the campaigns need, and the follow-through until it lands.
  • Campaign architecture, bidding, targeting, conversion signals, exclusions, tracking, and testing discipline.
  • Testing new inventory and platforms with a clear hypothesis and a point where you stop.

What Great Looks Like

jobs.title: Sales Development Representative (Phone-First)
jobs.description:
About the Company

Forager.ai is a bootstrapped B2B data company. We are the industry-leading people and contact data provider (mobile numbers, personal and work email, and people/company graphs), made available through API and data feeds to sales, recruiting and data platforms that build our data into their own products, and increasingly to go-to-market teams directly. We are a fully remote team of about ten people with historically very little turnover.

About the Role

This is a phone-first role. Email and LinkedIn outreach at Forager is automated and run by our Growth team, so the SDR does the part a machine cannot: get prospects on the phone, qualify them properly, and hand our closers meetings that turn into real opportunities. You will work directly with the CEO, Head of Growth, GTM agency, and our commercial Account Executive (AE).

Why join

  • Sell a product with a real edge: we’re the #1 mobile and personal email provider on Clay
    • Shoulder-to-shoulder training from our current SDR, plus regular coaching using call recordings
    • Learn one of the most advanced AI-driven outbound setups in the industry


What you will do

  • Respond quickly to inbound leads (demo requests from our website, data requests from marketplaces, and partner and referral introductions). Speed-to-lead is one of your key metrics
    • Run qualification calls with inbound and outbound leads: use case, data need and volume, budget, buying process and timeline. Route each lead to the right closer, or to self-service when that is the better fit.
    • Cold call the accounts our signal engine flags each sprint (our Tier 1 and Tier 2 target accounts), and book qualification calls and demos from those conversations.
    • Book meetings that closers accept. A demo counts as "Demo Accepted" when the AE has reviewed your call notes and agreed the opportunity is qualified. Demo Accepted is your core metric and drives your variable pay.
    • Bring what you learn back to the sprint review with Growth and Sales: which objections come up, which messaging lands, which signals convert.
    • Keep HubSpot accurate on every lead you touch. AI drafts the notes, enrichment and follow-ups; you confirm the facts and the next step.

What you will NOT spend your time on

  • Writing and sending email or LinkedIn sequences. These are automated and owned by the Growth team; you see the replies, not the sends.
    • Building lists or researching accounts. The signal engine and AI do this before a name reaches your call list.
    • Manual CRM data entry, call notes and meeting prep. AI drafts these; you check them.

Tools and systems

  • HubSpot: CRM, lead routing, deal stages and the Demo Accepted gate

• Parallel dialer for outbound calling

  • Automated email and LinkedIn software with sequences whose replies land with you
    • Call recording software, used for coaching and for AI call notes
    • AI assistants for account research, call summaries, CRM updates and follow-up drafts

Requirements

Must-haves:

  • Previous experience in a phone-heavy B2B SDR, BDR or inside sales role, ideally 2+ years
    • A cold-calling track record you can show: daily dial and connect volumes, meetings booked, and opportunities your sales team accepted that started with your cold call
    • Strong qualification skills: you know how to uncover need, budget and decision process, and you never leave a call without a next step
    • Clear, confident spoken English and comfort with technical buyers (product, data and engineering leaders)
    • Comfortable learning technical products quickly; you’ll explain enrichment APIs and data feeds to technical buyers
    • Self-managed and comfortable working in a fully remote team.

Nice-to-haves:

  • You have sold B2B data, sales technology, recruiting technology or developer and data infrastructure
    • You have experience with a parallel dialer, and HubSpot
    • You have worked marketplace or partner-sourced leads

Benefits

• Full-time contractor role

  • Fully remote. Any location, with a daily calling window of at least four hours between 9am and 6pm US Eastern.
    • Base pay plus variable, split roughly 70/30. Variable is paid on Demo Accepted meetings, not on meetings booked
    • Untracked PTO: take the time off you need, with no accrual to count. We trust you to get the job done

    Sound like you? Apply with your CV and a 2-minute audio or video recording about a cold call you made that turned into an opportunity your sales team accepted: what you said, the objection you hit, how you knew it was worth a meeting, and what happened after the handoff . We review every application, and our recruiter will be in touch within a few days to walk you through next steps!

jobs.title: Freight Dispatcher — Load Evaluation & Planning
jobs.description:
Freight Dispatcher — Load Evaluation & Planning

Full-Time | Remote — United States | U.S. Freight Operations

Evaluate the Load Before the Truck Commits

We are hiring a Freight Dispatcher — Load Evaluation & Planning to support U.S. trucking operations with a focus on freight evaluation, load selection, mileage analysis, trip feasibility, and day-to-day dispatch support.

This position may be a strong fit for transportation professionals, including experienced or former CDL-A drivers, who understand that the advertised freight rate is only one part of determining whether a load makes operational sense.

Previous employment specifically under the title of Freight Dispatcher is not required. Applicants must have relevant U.S. trucking, transportation, logistics, fleet, or closely related operational experience.

Load Evaluation

  • Search DAT One, Truckstop, or comparable U.S. freight load boards for available freight.
  • Compare available loads by lane, equipment type, rate, mileage, appointments, and operating requirements.
  • Calculate loaded miles, deadhead miles, total trip miles, and rate per mile.
  • Evaluate whether pickup and delivery schedules are operationally realistic.
  • Consider driver location, available Hours of Service, equipment, routing, weather, and freight requirements.
  • Identify excessive deadhead, unrealistic transit times, equipment conflicts, or other operational concerns.
  • Compare available freight options before presenting suitable loads for authorized review.

Trip & Freight Planning

  • Evaluate how a proposed load affects the driver's current location and subsequent freight opportunities.
  • Review pickup and delivery appointment requirements.
  • Consider available driver hours when evaluating trip feasibility.
  • Identify potential detention exposure, scheduling conflicts, or inefficient freight movements.
  • Assist with planning freight around equipment availability and operating requirements.
  • Present appropriate freight options for authorized review and booking.
  • Negotiate freight rates only when specifically authorized.

Driver & Broker Communication

  • Communicate professionally with U.S. CDL-A drivers, freight brokers, shippers, receivers, and authorized transportation personnel.
  • Confirm freight details, appointments, equipment requirements, and applicable operating instructions.
  • Clarify incomplete or inconsistent load information before presenting freight for approval.
  • Communicate accurate load information to drivers.
  • Monitor applicable freight updates and operational changes.
  • Escalate safety, compliance, broker-verification, documentation, or service concerns when appropriate.

Transportation Documentation

  • Maintain accurate load and dispatch records.
  • Review rate confirmations for consistency with agreed freight information.
  • Organize bills of lading, proof-of-delivery documents, and related transportation records.
  • Document appointment changes, delays, detention, layover, and applicable freight exceptions.
  • Maintain accurate communication histories and operational notes.
  • Identify missing information requiring follow-up.

Required Transportation Background

Relevant professional experience may include:

  • CDL-A truck driving
  • Freight dispatch support
  • Fleet operations
  • Carrier operations
  • Transportation coordination
  • Logistics operations
  • Freight brokerage support
  • Load planning
  • Owner-Operator operations
  • Comparable U.S. trucking operations

Required Skills

  • Working knowledge of U.S. trucking and freight operations.
  • Familiarity with U.S. freight load boards.
  • Ability to evaluate freight based on rate, mileage, deadhead, equipment, and appointments.
  • Ability to calculate loaded mileage, deadhead mileage, total trip mileage, and rate per mile.
  • Understanding of common CDL-A equipment types.
  • Understanding of pickup and delivery appointments.
  • Working knowledge of driver Hours-of-Service considerations.
  • Ability to identify operationally unsuitable freight.
  • Fluent professional spoken and written English.
  • Strong professional telephone and email communication.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail.
  • Computer and spreadsheet proficiency.
  • Reliable computer and stable high-speed internet connection.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.

Work Arrangement & Schedule

This is a full-time remote position supporting U.S. freight operations.

Primary hiring location: Chicago, Illinois, United States.
Hiring market: Remote — United States.

Qualified applicants may be considered throughout the United States.

jobs.title: Human Resources - HR & HRIS Operations Administrator
jobs.description:
Position Description:

Infinite Electronics is seeking an HRIS Analyst to serve as the primary configuration owner of our Dayforce environment. This is a fully remote, hands-on role for someone who has configured Dayforce across multiple modules and can translate a business policy into a working system rule.

Infinite implemented Dayforce recently, and the modules today are largely siloed and under-leveraged. Significant functionality we are already licensed for, including Compensation Management, Performance Management, and Succession Planning, is not yet in production. Numerous processes remain manual and external to the system.

This role owns closing that gap. The successful candidate will interview stakeholders, understand how hiring, compensation, payroll, and reporting actually work at Infinite, and then configure Dayforce to support those processes rather than force workarounds around it. This is ongoing work, not a one-time project. New policies, acquisitions, and business changes will require continuous reconfiguration, and this role is the durable internal capability for that.

The position carries both build and run responsibility. Alongside configuration work, it provides ongoing system support for the recurring processes that run through Dayforce, including weekly payroll and the annual Open Enrollment, Performance Management, and Compensation Review cycles. The successful candidate will be accountable for ensuring each cycle is configured, tested, and ready before it opens, and for resolving system issues while it is live.

General Duties and Responsibilities:

Serve as primary administrator and configuration owner for Dayforce across subscribed modules, including Core HR, Payroll, Time & Attendance, Benefits, Recruiting, Onboarding, and Compensation Management.

Translate business and policy requirements into Dayforce configuration, including pay rules, earning and deduction codes, eligibility rules, workflows, forms, and approval chains.

Diagnose incorrect system behavior by isolating the responsible rule, policy, or configuration element, and implement and validate the fix.

Lead deployment of licensed but unimplemented modules, including Compensation Management, Performance Management, and Succession Planning.

Design, test, and migrate configuration changes through the full release cycle, including regression testing against payroll and time results before production promotion.

Administer security roles, user access, and data governance, maintaining appropriate segregation of duties across HR, Payroll, and Finance.

Build and maintain reporting and dashboards for HR, Finance, and leadership, and improve data quality and consistency across modules.

Manage integrations between Dayforce and downstream systems, including benefit carriers, retirement recordkeepers, and Finance, and monitor interface errors.

Evaluate and test Dayforce quarterly releases, assess impact to existing configuration, and communicate changes to affected stakeholders.

Provide system ownership and support for weekly payroll processing, validating configuration-driven results, resolving calculation and rule issues, and supporting Payroll through pre-commit review and close.

Configure and administer annual Open Enrollment in Dayforce Benefits, including plan year setup, rates, eligibility and life event rules, enrollment workflows, employee-facing content, and carrier file updates, and provide support throughout the enrollment window.

Configure and run the annual Performance Management cycle, including review forms, rating scales, routing and approval workflows, calibration support, and cycle reporting.

Configure and administer the Annual Compensation Review in Dayforce Compensation Management, including merit and bonus cycle setup, budgets, eligibility rules, guidelines, manager worksheets, approval routing, and downstream loading of approved changes.

Maintain the recurring HR systems calendar and ensure configuration for each cycle is built, tested, and validated in advance of the cycle opening.

Partner with HR Operations and Payroll to identify manual and off-system processes and systematically move them into Dayforce.

Document configuration decisions, business rules, test plans, and standard operating procedures so the environment is supportable and auditable.

Serve as escalation point for complex system issues and manage tickets and enhancement requests with Dayforce support and managed services.

Education & Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field. Required.

Minimum of three years of hands-on Dayforce configuration experience across multiple modules. Required. Experience limited to end-user or reporting access does not meet this requirement.

Demonstrated ability to translate a written business policy into working system configuration and validate the result.

Working knowledge of payroll mechanics, including pay rules, earning and deduction codes, and how configuration drives calculation outcomes.

Experience managing configuration through a structured test and release process, including regression testing prior to production.

Experience building reports and resolving data integrity issues across integrated HR modules.

Experience supporting recurring operational cycles in an HCM platform, such as payroll processing, open enrollment, performance reviews, or a merit cycle.

Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to work independently and own problems to resolution.

Sound judgment handling confidential compensation and employee data.

Preferred Qualifications:

Dayforce implementation or post-implementation optimization experience.

Configuration experience running annual Open Enrollment, Performance Management, or Compensation Review cycles in Dayforce.

Experience with Dayforce Integration Studio, report writing, or API-based integrations.

Experience in a multi-entity organization or supporting acquisition integration into an existing HCM environment.

Hands-on multi-state payroll processing experience.

Dayforce certification in one or more modules.

Physical Job Requirements:

Ability to work in a remote or office-based setting using standard office equipment, computers, and job-related technology platforms.

Ability to communicate effectively with employees, managers, vendors, and internal stakeholders in virtual and in-person settings.

Ability to view, interpret, and analyze information on screens, documents, and reports for extended periods.

Ability to work extended or adjusted hours as required by payroll close, quarter-end, year-end, and system release cycles.

Reports To: Head of Total Rewards & HRIS

Environment: This role is performed remotely within the United States, with regular virtual collaboration across HR, Payroll, Finance, and Operations. Workload is cyclical. The position requires availability during weekly payroll processing windows, Dayforce release cycles, scheduled configuration deployments, and the annual Open Enrollment, Performance Management, and Compensation Review periods, which carry elevated workload and fixed deadlines.

Accommodation: Infinite Electronics is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with applicable law. An individual must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Infinite Electronics is an Equal Opportunity Employer and makes employment decisions based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to any status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
