jobs.title: PPC Marketing Specialist
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.title: Go-to-Market Strategy Intern
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Our teams work closely across product, engineering, customer success, sales, and company leadership to bring new capabilities to market and continuously improve the platform.

At Bask, product marketing plays an important role in connecting what we build with the businesses that use it. We value clear communication, a strong understanding of our customers, and the ability to turn complex product capabilities into practical value.

About the Role

We're looking for a Go-to-Market Strategy Intern to support market research, competitive analysis, customer segmentation, and go-to-market planning across Bask Health's software platform.

This internship is designed for someone interested in business strategy, technology, product marketing, and how software companies identify and reach customers.

You'll gain hands-on experience researching markets, evaluating commercial opportunities, and supporting the planning behind product launches and customer acquisition initiatives.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform connects merchant tools, website creation, clinical and pharmacy workflows, AI-enabled features, analytics, and monetization capabilities.

As a Go-to-Market Strategy Intern, you'll help our team understand which customer segments may benefit from different platform capabilities and how those capabilities should be communicated.

You'll work with product marketing and collaborate with product managers, sales, growth marketing, customer success, finance, and other internal stakeholders.

A major part of this internship will involve researching market opportunities and organizing information that helps the team make better commercial decisions.

You'll research the needs of entrepreneurs, e-commerce businesses, healthcare providers, and organizations interested in launching telehealth businesses.

You'll help identify the business challenges, purchasing considerations, and product requirements that influence customer decisions.

You'll conduct competitive research on telehealth infrastructure, B2B SaaS, e-commerce enablement, and related software markets.

You'll compare competitor positioning, target audiences, product offerings, and publicly available commercial information.

You'll help organize your findings into market research reports, competitive summaries, spreadsheets, and presentations.

You'll support customer segmentation research by identifying differences between potential customer groups.

You'll help the team understand how product messaging and go-to-market approaches may need to change across those groups.

You'll assist with preparing go-to-market plans for new product capabilities, including research, target audiences, messaging considerations, and launch deliverables.

You'll work with product managers to understand upcoming features and their potential commercial applications.

You'll collaborate with sales teams to understand customer objections, purchasing motivations, and common questions.

You'll also work with customer success teams to gather insights about customer adoption, business challenges, and product value.

You'll help research potential distribution channels, partnerships, and customer acquisition approaches.

You'll support the preparation of strategic presentations and internal planning documents.

You'll help track launch initiatives and organize information about project timelines, stakeholders, and deliverables.

You'll gain exposure to how SaaS companies think about customer acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion.

You'll assist with reviewing available performance data and summarizing trends that may inform future marketing initiatives.

You'll also learn how product marketing, sales, and growth teams coordinate to introduce software products to different audiences.

This internship is focused on supporting strategy development and research, rather than independently making pricing decisions or owning commercial agreements.

You'll have opportunities to contribute ideas, test assumptions through research, and present findings to relevant team members.

We're looking for someone who is analytical, organized, curious about business models, and comfortable working with both qualitative and quantitative information.

You should enjoy investigating questions, identifying patterns, and communicating findings clearly.

This is an opportunity to gain practical experience in go-to-market strategy while learning how a growing software platform evaluates markets and introduces products to customers.

What You'll Do

  • Support go-to-market strategy research across Bask Health's software platform.
  • Research target markets and potential customer segments.
  • Analyze customer needs, business challenges, and purchasing considerations.
  • Conduct competitive research on SaaS, telehealth, and e-commerce platforms.
  • Compare competitor positioning, target audiences, and product offerings.
  • Organize market research findings into reports and presentations.
  • Assist with developing customer segmentation frameworks.
  • Research potential use cases for different platform capabilities.
  • Support the preparation of go-to-market plans for product launches.
  • Help identify target audiences for new product features.
  • Assist with developing launch briefs and strategic planning documents.
  • Collaborate with product marketing on positioning research.
  • Work with product managers to understand new features and customer value.
  • Gather insights from sales about customer objections and purchasing motivations.
  • Collect customer feedback from customer success teams.
  • Research potential customer acquisition and distribution channels.
  • Assist with evaluating partnership and market expansion opportunities.
  • Support competitive differentiation research.
  • Help prepare internal strategic presentations.
  • Maintain market research spreadsheets and competitive tracking documents.
  • Organize launch timelines, deliverables, and stakeholder feedback.
  • Assist with reviewing customer acquisition and adoption metrics.
  • Help summarize commercial performance trends.
  • Research industry developments affecting SaaS and telehealth businesses.
  • Support analysis of customer segments and potential growth opportunities.
  • Document research assumptions, findings, and limitations.
  • Contribute ideas for improving go-to-market approaches.
  • Present research findings and recommendations to relevant team members.
  • Complete assigned strategic research projects and communicate progress.

Requirements

  • Currently pursuing a degree, recently graduated, or developing early professional experience in Business, Marketing, Economics, Finance, Strategy, Analytics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong interest in go-to-market strategy and technology businesses.
  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to research markets and organize information.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to summarize complex findings clearly.
  • Comfortable working with spreadsheets and presentations.
  • Basic understanding of business and marketing concepts or willingness to learn.
  • Interest in customer segmentation and market research.
  • Ability to work with qualitative and quantitative information.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Good organizational and time management skills.

About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Our teams work closely across product, engineering, customer success, sales, and company leadership to bring new capabilities to market and continuously improve the platform.

At Bask, product marketing plays an important role in connecting what we build with the businesses that use it. We value clear communication, a strong understanding of our customers, and the ability to turn complex product capabilities into practical value.

About the Role

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager, Clinical & Pharmacy Platform to develop product positioning, support go-to-market initiatives, and help customers understand Bask Health's clinical and pharmacy software capabilities.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform connects patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

As a Product Marketing Manager, you'll help communicate how Bask Health supports the operational workflows involved in running a telehealth business.

You'll work closely with product managers, engineers, pharmacy operations, sales, customer success, and other internal stakeholders to turn technical product functionality into clear customer-facing messaging.

This role requires someone who can learn complex software, ask detailed questions, and explain how different capabilities work together.

You'll develop messaging for patient intake, questionnaires, clinical workflows, electronic medical records, pharmacy integrations, prescription routing, and related operational features.

You'll help prospective customers understand how Bask Health connects patient-facing experiences with the systems that support clinical and pharmacy operations.

You'll also support messaging for new features and improvements across the clinical and pharmacy platform.

A major part of this role will involve creating accurate product marketing materials that make complicated workflows easier to understand.

You'll collaborate with product teams to learn how features function, what customer problems they solve, and how they should be communicated.

You'll work with technical and operational stakeholders to verify product details before publishing customer-facing materials.

You'll help coordinate product launches, prepare messaging, and ensure relevant teams understand new capabilities.

You'll develop product overviews, sales presentations, launch materials, customer education resources, and website content.

You'll partner with sales teams to understand the questions customers ask when evaluating telehealth software and healthcare infrastructure.

You'll use that feedback to improve product messaging and develop materials that address common questions and objections.

You'll also collaborate with customer success teams to support onboarding, feature education, and product adoption.

You'll conduct customer and market research to understand how healthcare businesses evaluate software platforms and what operational challenges influence their decisions.

You'll research competing healthcare technology platforms and help identify opportunities for stronger differentiation.

Because Bask Health operates in healthcare-related environments, accuracy is especially important. You'll work with appropriate internal reviewers when messaging involves clinical, pharmacy, or compliance-sensitive functionality.

You'll help maintain consistent terminology across product marketing materials and customer communications.

You'll support the measurement of product marketing performance through launch results, customer feedback, feature adoption, and other relevant indicators.

We're looking for someone who is organized, curious about healthcare technology, comfortable collaborating across teams, and able to take ownership of product marketing projects from planning through execution.

jobs.description:
FlowFuse is the enterprise platform that bridges physical assets and enterprise IT. Built on Node-RED, it lets industrial teams unify real-time data through workflows, AI agents, and industrial applications, extending rigid vendor systems with a low-code agility layer that adapts without rip-and-replace. Our customers run factories, energy grids, and supply chains on what we ship. When we get the platform wrong, a production line feels it.

We need someone to own the FlowFuse platform outright: the solution-agnostic foundation every customer solution is built on. That means enterprise management, edge and cloud deployment, industrial connectivity, industrial data modeling and contextualization, security, operator experience, and the reusable AI/ML capabilities that will set us apart. You decide where the platform goes over the next few years, and you write the work that gets it there.

This is not a roadmap-from-30,000-feet job. You will learn our customers and the industrial IoT (IIoT) space cold, then turn that knowledge into shipped platform capabilities that customers and our Solutions Engineering team reuse instead of rebuilding. You own the platform end to end: vision, roadmap, backlog, prioritization, refinement, and the GitHub issues your engineers actually build from. The tickets have to be exacting and technical. The work is hands-on and often unglamorous. You do it yourself before you ever hand it off.

If that sounds like the part of Product you'd rather skip, this isn't the role. If it sounds like the part you've been missing, keep reading.

What you'll actually do

  • Own the platform roadmap. Hold the multi-year, solution-agnostic view, then break it into work that ships this sprint. Decide where to invest beyond today's customer requests, and what to build, integrate, or source through partners. Track where industrial software and our competitors are heading, and decide where FlowFuse can establish meaningful differentiation.
  • Run the field-to-platform loop. Partner with Solutions Engineering to spot product gaps and recurring patterns in customer deployments. Decide what becomes a platform capability, what stays in the solution library, and what remains customer-specific. The goal: field-developed work becomes repeatable enterprise solutions, not unicorns we rebuild for every customer.
  • Learn our customers and the IIoT domain fast, then keep learning. Run continuous discovery. Sit in on sales and customer calls, mine the recordings in Fathom for the problem behind the request, and talk to users directly.
  • Make industrial data a first-class part of the platform. Lead the direction for industrial data modeling and contextualization: data models defined once and enforced across instances and sites, and the relationships between machines, processes, production events, decisions, and outcomes that our workflows and AI build on. AI readiness starts here.
  • Shape AI/ML in the platform. Lead the product direction for reusable AI/ML capabilities (AI-assisted development, agentic workflows, industrial data reasoning, machine vision integration), with clear judgment about what's production-ready versus a promising demo.
  • Make the platform enterprise-ready. Make it easier for customers and solution engineers to build, deploy, govern, and operate distributed Node-RED applications across many sites, mixed equipment, and cloud or self-hosted environments.
  • Run the lane day to day. Triage the backlog and every new idea that flies in, prioritize ruthlessly, sequence it, and get it into sprints.
  • Write GitHub issues your engineers respect. Precise, technical, unambiguous, with testable acceptance criteria. They should never have to guess what "done" means.
  • Run refinement with engineering. Show up prepared, make the calls, unblock fast, and validate outcomes after release.
  • Know the split. Product owns the roadmap, the what, and the why, and writes the issues. Engineering owns the how, technical design, and delivery estimates. Scope and sequencing tradeoffs are made together. There's no classic PM / designer / engineer trio here. It's mostly you and the engineers.
  • Wear other hats. This is a small startup. Some weeks the highest-leverage thing you can do isn't in your job description. You do it anyway.

The harder part of the job

Leadership here moves fast and thinks out loud. Ideas arrive at high volume and high velocity, from the CEO, our investors, your peers, and the live customer deals sales is racing to close. Part of the job is to be the filter and the translation layer. Absorb that energy, turn it into a clear and sequenced plan, and protect the engineering team's focus so they can do their best work. You don't pass chaos through. You stop it at your desk.

You'll partner closely with Solutions Engineering, who own customer solutions, industry-specific applications, and solution packaging. They are your most important internal customer. A big part of being effective is turning their field requests into platform capabilities that serve many solutions, not one, without the team feeling whiplash.

You'll also work with our CTO on technical direction and the Node-RED ecosystem. The CTO leads the Node-RED open-source project. You can advocate for upstream changes, but you don't own that project.

You report to the VP of Engineering and Product. You work with the engineering team, not against it. Earning their trust is the job, not a nice-to-have.

Where this goes

You start as a product team of one, owning the platform and doing the groundwork yourself. You may stay a team of one for a while, and we'd rather say that up front. From day one, you bring a point of view on where the platform should go. We're hiring someone to shape the plan, not just execute the one they inherit. Prove you can run it, and the path opens: take on more of the product surface, build and lead a product team, and help shape the wider product vision for FlowFuse. This scope is additive, not a graduation. A bigger title doesn't mean your baseline changes, at least not until you've built a team. We're putting that in writing because we mean it.

Your first 90 days

  • Day 30. You know the platform, its backlog, and our biggest customer commitments. You're fluent in the tools we run on (GitHub, Slack, Asana, Claude, Google Workspace) and working in them daily. You've sat in on refinements and written tickets to the standard we expect. You've met Solutions Engineering, sales, and marketing, and you know who owns what.
  • Day 60. You own the platform backlog and a published, prioritized roadmap. Your engineers trust your tickets enough to stop asking what you meant. You've stood up the field-to-platform intake process with Solutions Engineering and made real calls on what becomes platform and what doesn't.
  • Day 90. You've shipped a multi-week platform effort that solved a real customer problem and is reused beyond one deployment. You've set baselines for reuse, time-to-value, adoption, and reliability, and picked the first one or two AI/ML opportunities with a validation plan. You're the person everyone goes to for the state of the platform.

Your first year

  • Platform capabilities shipped and reused across multiple customer deployments, not rebuilt in the field.
  • Field-developed solutions turned into repeatable enterprise offerings.
  • Measurable reductions in onboarding effort, deployment effort, and solution delivery time against your 90-day baselines.
  • A credible long-term platform strategy alongside an always execution-ready near-term roadmap.

What we're looking for

  • A bias toward action. You move fast, ship, and show your work. You'd rather make a reversible call today than schedule a meeting about it next week.
  • Evidence you can do the craft. You've owned a backlog, written engineering-ready specs and tickets, and shipped capabilities that got adopted. We'll ask to see it (more below).
  • Strategic product vision and competitive foresight. You can look three to five years out and explain where industrial software, data, and AI are heading, what competitors are building, and what that means for what we build, partner for, or avoid. Show us a time your read of the market changed a roadmap.
  • Industrial depth, or proof you learn hard domains fast. Experience in manufacturing, industrial automation, or IIoT, and an understanding of how OT, plant-floor systems, and enterprise IT intersect, is a strong plus. So is a track record of going deep on something hard, with receipts. We've hired the experienced-on-paper version before. It didn't ship.
  • Platform experience. You've shipped B2B platforms, infrastructure, developer tools, or similarly technical products, and you've found reusable capabilities inside customer-specific work.
  • Fluency with engineers. You speak their language, respect their constraints, and make their lives easier, not harder.
  • AI/ML product judgment. Experience taking AI/ML or LLM-powered capabilities from concept to adoption, ideally at the edge or in industrial settings, is a strong plus. At minimum, you can tell a production-ready capability from a promising demo.
  • Fluent with AI tools. You already use them to draft specs, prototype, and move faster, and you're hungry for better ways to work. We run on this stuff. You should too.
  • Spine. You coach people toward their best work, hold a firm line on guardrails, and when someone won't improve, you make the hard call. Tough and fair. People who listen do their best work with you.
  • A taste for startups specifically. If you thrive on predictability, you'll be miserable here. If ambiguity energizes you, you'll thrive. Don't worry, we at least have processes we all agreed to.
  • People management experience is welcome but not required to start. Tell us honestly what you've done and what you want next. We’re growing and we want you to, too.
  • Familiarity with Node-RED or open-source ecosystems is a plus.
  • We're hiring for the right person, not a fixed title. A strong mid-level PM ready to own an area, a senior PM who wants back into the hands-on craft — even someone whose sights are set on Director. Whoever you are, you start in the same seat: owning an area and doing the work yourself. Experienced or not, that's the baseline, and it's non-negotiable. Earn it here and the scope opens fast (see "Where this goes"). Tell us where you are and we'll meet you there.

Logistics

  • Remote-only and async-first. We default to writing things down. Engineering sits mostly in Europe; customer-facing teams are in the US and Europe. This role is open to candidates in the United States or Europe.Working hours are flexible, but we appreciate overlap with West Coast US. We'll hire almost anywhere we can legally (a few countries excepted).
  • Compensation. Competitive base, calibrated to your level, plus meaningful equity.
  • Unlimited paid time off. We mean it, and the team actually takes it.
  • What you'll live in. FlowFuse, Node-RED, GitHub Issues and Projects, Hubspot, PostHog, Slack, Asana, and Google Meet.

jobs.title: Paid Social Director
jobs.description:
The Shipyard is a leading, independent marketing and communication agency headquartered in Columbus, OH and San Diego, CA that brings together talented individuals across the creative, communications, media and digital landscape. Uniquely designed to Engineer Brand Love through a unifying approach of paid, owned and earned channels, we work together to grow brands that audiences can't help but love.

Our family of brands, Fahlgren Mortine, TURNER and TinyWins, span integrated communications, travel and lifestyle, and digital innovation, giving us the range and depth to deliver for clients locally, regionally and nationally.

Momentum is nothing without the people driving it. See who we are at before you hit apply!

SUMMARY

We are looking for a smart, experienced, and motivated Paid Social Director to join our team.

The Social Director is the senior-most leader of the paid social practice at The Shipyard. This role exists to set the vision for how Shipyard approaches paid social — establishing the strategic and technical standard, developing the talent pipeline, driving the growth of client relationships, and ensuring the social team consistently delivers work that is best-in-class.

A great Social Director doesn't just oversee campaigns — they define what great paid social looks like for the entire team and for the agency. They are a trusted strategic advisor to clients, a visible expert in the social marketplace, and a leader who makes everyone around them better.

At The Shipyard, we know that it's your unique talents, backgrounds, and perspectives that make you who you are, just like our team, who come from various career paths and experiences. We believe we can't be truly diverse without you bringing your most authentic self to the agency.

Studies show that people from marginalized communities may not always apply for positions if they don't meet every single requirement in a job posting. At The Shipyard, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the requirements. We believe that your passion for what we stand for — our values and purpose — is just as important as meeting every checkbox.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Media Knowledge

The Social Director is the foremost paid social expert at the agency. Your knowledge is not just deep — it is visionary, and you use it to set the direction for how the team thinks, plans, and executes.

  • Possess and actively demonstrate expert, current, and forward-looking knowledge of the full paid social ecosystem — Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Snapchat, and emerging platforms — including platform algorithm dynamics, audience solutions, creative innovation, social commerce, creator monetization, and the evolving privacy and measurement landscape, and apply it to set the strategic direction for the social team
  • Define and evolve the standards for how social platforms and technology are used across the team — ensuring rigorous, sophisticated application that consistently delivers competitive advantage for clients
  • Serve as the senior-most steward of client investment within the paid social practice — ensuring budgets are managed responsibly, billing processes are accurate and timely across every account, and the team treats client spend with the same care they would their own
  • Lead the agency's thinking on social investment strategy, platform mix, budget allocation, and measurement — setting a high bar for how social campaigns are planned, executed, and evaluated
  • Serve as the agency's internal and external thought leader on paid social — bringing a clear, informed, and forward-thinking POV to client conversations, industry discussions, and new business opportunities
  • Proactively identify and evaluate emerging social platforms, creator economy shifts, social commerce developments, privacy changes, and industry disruptions — and translate them into clear strategic implications for clients and the agency
  • Build and maintain the agency's most strategic platform partnerships with Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, and others — negotiating at the highest level to secure preferential access, beta opportunities, and competitive intelligence that benefit clients across the portfolio

Strategic Thinking & Planning

The Social Director sets the strategic vision for the social team and ensures that sophisticated, insight-driven channel strategy is embedded in every campaign across the portfolio. This role creates a paid social practice that delivers on client solutions so effectively that it attracts spend and growth.

  • Set and own the strategic vision for paid social across the agency's client portfolio — ensuring every channel plan reflects a sophisticated audience strategy, a defensible platform mix and creative approach, and a measurable commitment to business outcomes
  • Bring a strong, informed point of view to the evolution of the agency’s social strategy frameworks, best practices, and optimization standards – partnering with the VP, Media Investment to ensure consistency, ambition, and continuous improvement across all accounts and team members
  • Lead the development of social strategy for the agency's most complex and high-value accounts — applying the highest level of strategic rigor to full-funnel, multi-platform social challenges
  • Drive a culture of insight-driven strategy across the social team — ensuring audience intelligence, creative performance data, and platform insights are consistently embedded in how the team plans, optimizes, and learns
  • Identify transformative strategic opportunities for clients — new platform approaches, creator strategies, social commerce applications, advanced measurement capabilities — and bring them forward with a compelling business case
  • Serve as the social strategic anchor in all cross-functional, new business, and client leadership contexts — ensuring social thinking actively elevates the overall media strategy across the agency

Communication

The Social Director is an exceptionally skilled communicator who can move a room, build client confidence, and inspire the social team. Your communication sets the tone for the entire practice.

  • Lead client presentations with authority, strategic depth, and the ability to connect social thinking to business outcomes in a way that earns trust and wins confidence
  • Develop and drive a communication standard for the social team — in presentations, in campaign reporting, and in day-to-day client interactions — that consistently reflects Shipyard's ambition and expertise
  • Communicate complex, multi-faceted social strategies to senior client stakeholders, C-suite audiences, and agency leadership clearly, persuasively, and memorably
  • Represent Shipyard's social capabilities and POV externally — in industry forums, new business contexts, and marketplace conversations — with confidence and conviction
  • Coach and develop strong communicators across the social team, from Coordinators through Associate Directors, ensuring communication excellence at every level

Partnership

The Social Director builds and leads the relationships across the agency's social practice — with clients, with platform partners, and across the integrated agency team.

  • Serve as the senior client social partner for the agency's highest-value accounts — building deep, trust-based partnerships rooted in strategic value and business impact
  • Manage agency relationships with key social platforms — Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Snapchat, and others — leveraging relationships to build preferential access and identifying opportunities that create meaningful competitive advantage across the client portfolio
  • Partner closely with media planning, analytics, creative, client engagement, and brand planning to drive integrated, outcome-focused work across the agency
  • Build a strong working relationship with the data and analytics team — ensuring social campaigns are grounded in data intelligence and that measurement is built into the work from the start, not bolted on at the end
  • Serve as a senior leader for the social practice in new business, agency growth, and industry contexts — building The Shipyard's reputation as a social leader in the marketplace
  • Model and champion a culture of partnership — across the social team, across the agency, and in the marketplace

Team Development

The Social Director is a committed people leader who builds a strong, capable social team. Building, developing, and retaining great social practitioners is among the most important things this role does.

  • Directly manage the social team, including hiring, onboarding, development, and performance management
  • Build and sustain a high-performing team culture defined by technical excellence, strategic rigor, intellectual curiosity, genuine collaboration, and a commitment to doing great work
  • Develop a strong bench of talent at every level — from Coordinator through Associate Director — ensuring the team is always growing toward the next level of capability
  • Set clear performance expectations and hold team members accountable with fairness, directness, and genuine care for their development
  • Serve as a mentor and career advisor to senior practitioners and Associate Directors, helping them develop the leadership skills and strategic vision to grow into the next generation of social leaders at Shipyard
  • Partner with the VP, Media Investment on workforce planning, talent acquisition strategy, and team structure to ensure the social practice is built for long-term success

WHAT YOU’LL GET

  • The overall target range of base compensation for this role is $135,000 - $150,000. Compensation offered will be determined by additional factors such as location and experience.
  • Open PTO
  • Paid sick time (in applicable states)
  • Flexible work hours
  • Paid holidays + holiday closure between Christmas Eve and New Year’s Day
  • Company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life insurance and disability benefits
  • 401k program with employer matching
  • 6 weeks paid parental leave
  • Employee bonus referrals
  • Dog-friendly offices
  • Company-provided snacks and beverages (yes, beer/wine included)
  • … and lots more!

Requirements

  • Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.

jobs.title: Frontend Engineering Intern
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Frontend Engineering Intern to join Bask Health's engineering team and gain hands-on experience building modern web applications.

This internship is designed for students, recent graduates, and aspiring software engineers who want to strengthen their frontend development skills while contributing to real product features. You'll work alongside experienced engineers, designers, and product managers to help build and improve the interfaces that power Bask's telehealth platform.

You'll contribute to frontend components, responsive layouts, forms, application workflows, and user interface improvements. Your projects may involve merchant dashboards, patient-facing experiences, storefronts, or internal applications used by Bask's teams.

You'll gain practical experience with technologies such as React, Next.js, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS while learning how professional engineering teams plan, develop, test, review, and deploy software.

This is a hands-on engineering internship, not an observational program. You'll write code, participate in development discussions, receive feedback through code reviews, and contribute to features that may be used in production.

We're looking for someone who enjoys programming, is eager to learn, and takes initiative when solving problems. You don't need previous professional experience, but you should have a basic understanding of frontend development and be able to demonstrate your interest through coursework, personal projects, or other hands-on experience.

What You'll Do

  • Assist with developing frontend features across Bask Health's web applications.
  • Work with experienced engineers to implement user interface components and application functionality.
  • Write frontend code using JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and Next.js.
  • Help build responsive interfaces using HTML, CSS, and modern frontend development techniques.
  • Develop reusable components for merchant-facing and internal applications.
  • Assist with implementing forms, navigation elements, buttons, modals, and other interactive components.
  • Translate design specifications and Figma files into working frontend interfaces.
  • Support improvements to merchant dashboards, storefronts, and patient-facing experiences.
  • Help connect frontend components to backend APIs and application data.
  • Assist with implementing basic application state and interactive functionality.
  • Learn how to handle user input, validation, and error messages.
  • Help identify and resolve frontend bugs and layout issues.
  • Test interfaces across different browsers and screen sizes.
  • Support accessibility and responsive design improvements.
  • Collaborate with designers to improve visual consistency and usability.
  • Learn and apply frontend coding standards and development best practices.
  • Write clean, readable, and maintainable code.
  • Assist with writing unit tests and checking frontend functionality.
  • Participate in code reviews and apply feedback from experienced engineers.
  • Use Git and established development workflows to manage code changes.
  • Help document reusable components and implementation details.
  • Participate in engineering discussions and team collaboration.
  • Learn how frontend applications interact with backend services.
  • Assist with improving application performance and loading behavior.
  • Explore new frontend technologies and development techniques when relevant.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools while reviewing and understanding generated code.
  • Complete assigned development tasks with guidance and gradually take on more responsibility.

Requirements

Requirements

  • Currently studying computer science, software engineering, web development, or a related field, or developing equivalent skills through bootcamps or independent learning.
  • Basic knowledge of JavaScript.
  • Familiarity with HTML and CSS.
  • Foundational understanding of how websites and web applications work.
  • Basic experience with React or another frontend framework through coursework or personal projects.
  • Interest in learning TypeScript and modern frontend development tools.
  • Understanding of fundamental programming concepts.
  • Familiarity with responsive web design principles.
  • Basic understanding of reusable UI components.
  • Willingness to learn how frontend applications communicate with APIs.
  • Familiarity with Git or willingness to learn version control.
  • Ability to write organized and readable code.
  • Basic problem-solving and debugging skills.
  • Attention to detail when implementing frontend interfaces.
  • Interest in user interface development and user experience.
  • Willingness to learn software testing and quality assurance practices.
  • Ability to follow technical instructions and development guidelines.
  • Strong curiosity and willingness to explore unfamiliar technologies.
  • Ability to ask questions and seek guidance when needed.
  • Openness to constructive feedback and code reviews.
  • Good communication and collaboration skills.
  • Ability to manage assigned tasks and communicate progress.
  • Willingness to learn professional software development workflows.
  • Genuine interest in building useful web applications.
  • Comfort collaborating with a remote engineering team.

Nice to Have

  • Personal projects demonstrating frontend development skills.
  • Coursework or projects involving React.
  • Familiarity with TypeScript.
  • Experience building applications with Next.js.
  • Familiarity with Tailwind CSS or comparable styling frameworks.
  • Experience translating Figma designs into working interfaces.
  • Familiarity with responsive layouts using Flexbox and CSS Grid.
  • Experience building forms or interactive web components.
  • Basic understanding of REST APIs.
  • Familiarity with browser developer tools.
  • Experience using GitHub for personal or collaborative projects.
  • Exposure to component libraries or design systems.
  • Familiarity with frontend state management concepts.
  • Experience writing basic unit tests.
  • Exposure to accessibility and semantic HTML.
  • Experience building a personal portfolio website.
  • Contributions to open-source or collaborative development projects.
  • Interest in e-commerce, SaaS, or healthcare technology.
  • Familiarity with frontend deployment platforms or CI/CD workflows.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor or Claude Code.

Career Category

Job Description


Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients


At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.


Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.


Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Director - Coverage, Contracts & Pricing

Amgen has an exciting opportunity for an individual looking to make a significant impact on the organization. As a member of the U.S. Value & Access team, this Coverage, Contracts & Pricing Director for the Lifecycle Value Lab (LVL) portfolio is integral to Amgen’s financial performance. The Director will lead pricing and contract strategy and performance activities for Nplate, Vectibix, Lumakras, Kyprolis, Aimovig, and Imlygic.


This role provides a strong foundation in the U.S. healthcare market and is a good avenue to many future commercial healthcare roles. The Coverage, Contracts & Pricing Director role is integrated into the brand leadership team and is part of the U.S. Value & Access Oncology Contracts & Pricing team which together provides excellent opportunities to grow into other Marketing and/or Value & Access areas of the company. Amgen offers robust training, education, and mentoring programs to ensure staff are successful.


Job Responsibilities:


The Coverage, Contracts & Pricing Director is responsible for all access strategies and tactics supporting the LVL portfolio of brands above. They will coordinate pricing, provider and payer contracting strategy assessments, conduct market research and analytics to inform strategies, implement strategies to sustain and improve coverage, and assess effectiveness of these strategies for continuous improvement. The role will lead a team responsible for coordinating access related needs across payer, site of infusion, and health care providers. In addition, the role is responsible to lead access needs for launches and managing competitive entrants. Additionally, there are opportunities to drive unique channel segment volume growth (e.g. hospital, U.S. government, e.g. Medicaid and Veteran’s Affairs), pricing and contracting strategies.


Key responsibilities also include:


    • Lead the development and analysis for pricing and contracting strategies (provider and payer), informing gross to net management and forecasting to optimize net sales
    • Evaluate and approve financial models to measure contract performance, inform price optimization and support discount forecasting
    • Maintain a comprehensive understanding of key customer’s financials, growth drivers, membership, mergers/acquisitions, end customers, etc.
    • Responsible for value story development, resourcing, payer segmentation & positioning, and coordinating training
    • Support ad-hoc requests by senior leadership for product and/or customer related business analytics which generate data-driven business insights, visualizations, and recommendations
    • Inform Pipeline, LCM, and LOE strategies
    • Coordination with Brand Leads (marketing & sales), Medical, Market Access Field Teams, Finance, Forecasting, Analytics, Global Value & Access, Patient Access & Reimbursement, HEOR/RWE, etc
    • Conduct Channel & Provider (e.g. SOC) Contracting assessments & recommendations, informing Site of Infusion Strategy & Net Cost Recovery, and Billing & Coding Requirements

Basic Qualifications:


    • Doctorate degree & 4 years of directly related experience, OR
    • Master's degree & 8 years of directly related experience OR
    • Bachelor’s degree & 10 years of directly related experience AND
    • In addition to meeting at least one of the above requirements, you must have at least 4 years experience directly managing people and/or leadership experience leading teams, projects, programs, or directing the allocation or resources. Your managerial experience may run concurrently with the required technical experience referenced above

Preferred Qualifications


    • Experience solving complex business problems
    • Advanced knowledge of pricing, contracting, and financial modeling, to include for medical benefit buy and bill infused products in Medicare, Commercial, Medicaid, and by site of infusion segment
    • Experience assisting in management of financial planning process, gross to net management, and forecasting
    • Demonstrated experience managing marketing process from insight generation, brand planning, budget allocation & management, development, training & execution of resources and messages, and a spirit of continuous improvement to meet brand and access needs
    • Demonstrated track record of increasing responsibility and leadership of both people and managing multiple projects concurrently
    • Previous experience providing and delivering information for decision making by executive management and executive communication skill
    • Strong orientation to teamwork; works collaboratively, effectively and efficiently with others in a matrixed team environment
    • Experience developing and driving adoption of new critical technology
    • Leadership experience, could be in your community, at work, or as part of your education
    • Advanced degree, e.g. MBA, Data Scientist, or equivalent experience preferred
    • Remote work available with 25-30% travel depending on brand, USVA, and organizational needs

What you can expect of us


As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.


The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.


In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

  • Stock-based long-term incentives

jobs.title: UX Writer, Intakes & Clinical Workflows
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a UX Writer, Intakes & Clinical Workflows to help create clear, accurate, and intuitive language throughout Bask Health's patient intake and healthcare-related software experiences.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform brings together patient questionnaires, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools.

As a UX Writer, you'll help patients and authorized platform users understand the information they need to provide, the steps they need to complete, and what to expect as they move through important healthcare-related workflows.

This is a hands-on product writing role focused on the language people encounter while completing intake questionnaires, navigating clinical processes, and interacting with forms that may contain sensitive or specialized information.

You'll write question labels, response options, instructions, helper text, validation messages, confirmation screens, and other interface content that makes complicated workflows easier to follow.

A major focus of this position will be patient intake questionnaires. You'll work on content for multi-step forms, conditional questions, required fields, and instructions that help patients provide information accurately.

You'll also support content within clinical and pharmacy-related workflows, collaborating with appropriate subject matter experts to ensure language reflects approved processes and terminology.

Unlike a general UX writing role, this position requires particular attention to precision. Small differences in wording can affect how users interpret a question, understand an instruction, or complete a workflow.

You'll work closely with product designers, product managers, engineers, content designers, and operational stakeholders to ensure interface language is integrated into the product development process.

You'll review prototypes, identify unclear or inconsistent language, and recommend improvements that make workflows easier to understand without changing the intended meaning of approved clinical content.

You'll also help maintain consistent terminology across questionnaires, patient experiences, and related administrative tools.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll need to approach privacy, patient comprehension, and clinical boundaries carefully. You'll work with authorized reviewers when content involves medical terminology, treatment-related information, consent, or other sensitive subjects.

You'll use usability feedback, research findings, and product observations to identify where confusing language contributes to errors, incomplete forms, or unnecessary support requests.

We're looking for someone who enjoys making complicated information easier to understand, has exceptional attention to detail, and can write concise, practical content for sensitive digital workflows.

What You'll Do

  • Write clear, accurate, and accessible UX content for patient intake questionnaires.
  • Develop question labels, instructions, helper text, and response options for digital forms.
  • Improve language throughout multi-step patient intake experiences.
  • Write content for conditional questions and branching questionnaire flows.
  • Create clear instructions for required fields and information requests.
  • Develop validation messages that help users correct incomplete or invalid responses.
  • Write error messages and recovery guidance for interrupted workflows.
  • Create confirmation messages and next-step instructions following questionnaire submission.
  • Help users understand the difference between submitting information and receiving subsequent clinical review.
  • Collaborate with product designers to improve the clarity of complex forms.
  • Review questionnaire prototypes to identify confusing or ambiguous wording.
  • Support content for approved clinical and pharmacy-related workflows.
  • Work with appropriate subject matter experts to validate specialized terminology.
  • Maintain consistent language across related questions and workflow steps.
  • Develop reusable writing patterns for common questionnaire interactions.
  • Contribute to UX writing standards and content guidelines.
  • Apply plain-language principles to patient-facing instructions.
  • Support accessible content for users with different reading and comprehension needs.
  • Work with product managers to understand content requirements and workflow objectives.
  • Collaborate with engineers to ensure interface copy is implemented accurately.
  • Review how content behaves within conditional and dynamically generated forms.
  • Partner with UX researchers to evaluate question comprehension and task completion.
  • Incorporate usability feedback into writing improvements.
  • Identify wording that may unintentionally influence or confuse user responses.
  • Support consistent terminology across configurable merchant questionnaires.
  • Document writing decisions and terminology recommendations.
  • Participate in design reviews and content quality checks before release.
  • Own assigned UX writing projects from initial requirements through implementation and iteration.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional experience in UX writing, content design, product writing, or a closely related field.
  • Portfolio or writing samples demonstrating UX writing for digital products.
  • Excellent writing, editing, and proofreading skills.
  • Experience writing content for web or mobile applications.
  • Strong understanding of user-centered writing principles.
  • Ability to simplify complicated information while preserving accuracy.
  • Experience writing form labels, instructions, helper text, and validation messages.
  • Familiarity with multi-step forms and complex digital workflows.
  • Understanding of plain-language communication principles.
  • Strong attention to terminology, consistency, and precise wording.
  • Experience collaborating with product designers and product managers.
  • Ability to work effectively with software engineers during implementation.
  • Familiarity with Figma or comparable collaborative design tools.
  • Understanding of accessibility and inclusive writing practices.
  • Experience maintaining consistent language across product experiences.
  • Familiarity with UX writing guidelines or content design systems.
  • Ability to review interfaces and identify ambiguous or confusing content.
  • Experience incorporating usability feedback into writing improvements.
  • Familiarity with user research and comprehension testing concepts.
  • Ability to communicate writing recommendations clearly.
  • Experience working with subject matter experts to validate specialized information.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple assignments.
  • Ability to balance user comprehension, product requirements, and technical constraints.
  • Experience working in cross-functional product development teams.
  • Ability to independently deliver accurate, high-quality UX writing.

Nice to Have

  • Experience writing UX content for healthcare or telehealth products.
  • Familiarity with patient intake questionnaires and medical forms.
  • Experience writing for clinical or pharmacy-related applications.
  • Understanding of healthcare terminology and patient communication needs.
  • Familiarity with health literacy and plain-language healthcare writing.
  • Experience working with clinicians, pharmacists, or healthcare operations teams.
  • Understanding of HIPAA and healthcare-related privacy considerations.
  • Experience writing for sensitive or high-stakes digital interactions.
  • Familiarity with consent-related interfaces and required acknowledgments.
  • Experience writing content for conditional questionnaires or branching workflows.
  • Understanding of questionnaire design and neutral question wording.
  • Experience supporting configurable or white-label SaaS platforms.
  • Familiarity with patient onboarding and eligibility-related workflows.
  • Experience contributing to terminology libraries or content style guides.
  • Understanding of WCAG accessibility guidelines.
  • Experience collaborating with researchers on comprehension testing.
  • Familiarity with structured content models and reusable interface strings.
  • Experience writing for complex administrative software.
  • Understanding of responsible AI communication in healthcare-related products.
  • Experience working in fast-moving, cross-functional product teams.

jobs.description:
Hey, I’m Avery, the CEO of Modash.

We’re working to help every creator earn a living. Nearly 3,000 brands around the world use Modash to discover, partner with and pay creators: from finding the right people to managing relationships, measuring campaigns and running affiliate programs.

I’m looking for a Web Product Manager to own the direction of our website and help more of the people who find Modash become customers.

Background & reason for hiring

Our website brings in millions of organic visitors each year. We have a strong foundation in SEO and content, talented people across design, marketing and engineering, and no shortage of ideas for what the website could do better.

But traffic alone isn’t enough. Today, that means:

  • Visitors arrive, but not enough of the right ones understand Modash and take the next step, whether that’s signing up or booking a demo.
  • Requests come from across the company, from both Platform and API, and nobody owns the call on what matters most for the website as a whole.
  • Without one owner, it’s hard for the team to prioritize and move as fast as it should.

The website serves our Platform, our API and teams across Modash. Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, SEO/AEO, Design and Engineering all contribute to it. I’m looking for someone who can treat the website like a product: build a vision for it, make choices based on evidence, and help a team turn those choices into results. This isn’t a job for someone who wants to manage a queue of requests without challenging them.

Scope of the role & some examples

Example 1: Giving the website a clear direction

  • Developing a vision and roadmap for web that supports both the Platform and API
  • Sitting with Platform and API stakeholders who both need website changes, understanding the business case for each, and deciding what the team should do first
  • Being clear about what waits or doesn’t get done, so people across Modash understand what the web team is working on and why

Example 2: Turning more of our traffic into customers

  • Looking at a high-traffic page that isn’t generating enough signups, working out why, and agreeing on an improvement with design and engineering
  • Working with Product Marketing on a page that makes a part of Modash easier to understand, then checking whether the change made a difference
  • Running experiments where useful and measuring the impact on signups, demo bookings and the quality of the customers we attract
  • Protecting the organic foundation that brings people to Modash in the first place

Example 3: Leading the people and work behind the website

  • Giving designers context and feedback on a problem without prescribing their solution, and trusting their expertise
  • Bringing marketing, product and engineering together to take work from an unclear problem through design, launch and learning
  • Reviewing how a page moves from brief to launch and fixing the parts of the process that slow people down
  • Working with technical partners on measurement and site quality, so we can move quickly without losing what makes the website effective

You won’t be writing every line of code or designing every page. But you’ll need to get close enough to the work to make good decisions and help the team move.

Team structure

You’ll work closely with designers and the people building the site, and partner with stakeholders across Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, SEO/AEO, Design and Engineering.

Requirements

Required skills and experience

  • You’ve owned a website or digital product with a clear business outcome. You can tell us what you changed, why you chose it and what happened.
  • You’ve improved a customer journey or conversion funnel using data, customer insight and experimentation.
  • You’ve set a direction and prioritized competing opportunities, including saying no when the team can’t do everything.
  • You’ve led or developed people and helped designers, engineers and marketers work well together. You give clear feedback and trust the specialists around you.
  • You’ve taken cross-functional work from an ambiguous problem through to launch and learning.
  • You’re comfortable with web analytics and the technical side of running a website. You don’t need to write the code, but you can have a useful conversation with the people who do.
  • You communicate decisions clearly to stakeholders with different goals.

Nice to haves:

  • B2B SaaS experience
  • Experience with organic acquisition
  • Experience with a website serving more than one product

More important than any of these is that you can understand our context, build a sensible plan and make it happen.

Benefits

What we’re offering

  • Fully remote working in Europe 🏠 As long as you have a reliable internet connection, work wherever is best for you. At home, in a café, on a beach. Whatever works.
  • Compensation 💰 Your compensation is made up of salary and stock options. As we’re growing fast, the stock option package is especially significant. Annual salary range is 70,000€ - 90,000€ for this role. We hire across Europe, so the exact number depends on your location, employment type, skills, and experience.
  • Flexible working hours ⏱ We trust you to do your job without anyone looking over your shoulder. Do your best work whenever it suits you.
  • Unlimited paid vacation 🌴 If you’re happy and well rested, you’ll do better work. Take the time you need to enjoy a balanced life.
  • Personal development 🧠 When you grow, we benefit. If there’s a course, book or conference that will help you upskill, we’ll cover it.
  • Ownership 💡 You’re the expert at what you do, so you should have the freedom to make decisions and act quickly. No unnecessary red tape. Got an out-of-the-box idea? You’ll have the autonomy to try things you might not be able to at other companies.
  • Regular team offsites ✈️ We’re remote-first, but we make time to connect, collaborate, and have fun together in person.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Evaluation & Reliability
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Evaluation & Reliability to design, build, and maintain the systems that measure and improve the quality of Bask Health's AI-powered applications.

As Bask introduces more AI capabilities across patient experiences, merchant tools, clinical workflows, and internal operations, we need reliable ways to understand how these systems perform. You'll help establish the engineering infrastructure, evaluation methods, and monitoring practices that allow teams to ship AI features with confidence.

This role sits at the intersection of machine learning engineering, software infrastructure, automated testing, and production reliability. You'll work on evaluation pipelines, benchmark datasets, regression testing, model monitoring, and tools that help engineers identify failures before they affect users.

You'll develop systems that measure more than whether an AI model produces a response. You'll help determine whether that response is accurate, relevant, grounded in appropriate information, consistent with application requirements, and safe for its intended use.

You'll also investigate production issues, identify patterns in model failures, and collaborate with applied AI engineers to improve prompts, retrieval systems, model configurations, and application behavior.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related workflows, reliability is especially important. You'll help establish safeguards for sensitive use cases, support human review where appropriate, and make sure AI systems are evaluated against clear quality expectations before deployment.

This is a hands-on senior engineering position with ownership over evaluation infrastructure and reliability practices. You'll contribute production code, design scalable testing systems, and help establish standards that other engineers can use across multiple AI applications.

We're looking for someone who enjoys turning complex machine learning behavior into measurable engineering systems and who understands that successful AI products depend on consistent performance, not just impressive demonstrations.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build evaluation infrastructure for AI and machine learning applications across Bask Health.
  • Develop automated testing systems for large language model applications and intelligent workflows.
  • Establish measurable quality standards for production AI features.
  • Create evaluation pipelines that assess accuracy, relevance, completeness, consistency, and reliability.
  • Build and maintain representative datasets for testing AI application behavior.
  • Develop regression testing systems to detect quality changes when models, prompts, or application logic are updated.
  • Design evaluation methods for retrieval-augmented generation and knowledge-grounded AI systems.
  • Measure retrieval quality, grounding accuracy, and unsupported model outputs.
  • Build tools for identifying hallucinations, incorrect reasoning, and unreliable responses.
  • Develop testing approaches for AI agents, tool calling, and multi-step workflows.
  • Evaluate whether AI systems follow application instructions and respect workflow boundaries.
  • Implement automated checks for structured outputs, API interactions, and tool execution.
  • Build monitoring systems that track AI performance in production.
  • Develop dashboards and reporting tools for model quality, latency, errors, and operational reliability.
  • Investigate production AI failures and identify their underlying technical causes.
  • Collaborate with applied AI engineers to improve prompts, retrieval pipelines, and model configurations.
  • Establish testing procedures for model upgrades and provider changes.

Administrative Operations

  • Understanding of municipal permitting in California or a comparable jurisdiction.

  • Strong prioritization, organization, and record-keeping skills with minimal supervision.

  • You follow through without needing reminders and take ownership of tasks until they are completed.

  • You remain calm and organized when multiple priorities require attention at the same time.

Afternoons are typically focused on production coordination, confirming crew schedules, flagging material needs, and making sure upcoming roofing projects have everything in place before work begins.

Role Overview

We are looking for a highly organised, dependable and proactive Personal Assistant to provide personal and family administrative support to an Operations Director.

This is not a traditional Executive Assistant or business-support position. The primary purpose of the role is to take ownership of day-to-day personal administration, household scheduling and family logistics, helping ensure that commitments are well organised, communicated and followed through.

The ideal person will be trustworthy, discreet and exceptionally organised, with the confidence to manage multiple diaries, appointments and practical arrangements independently.

  • Manage personal appointments and general life administration.

  • Keep track of important personal deadlines, renewals and recurring commitments.

Household & Family Logistics

  • Coordinate vehicle-related administration including servicing, MOTs, repairs, insurance renewals and appointments.

  • Coordinate household appointments, maintenance visits and service providers when required.

About You

You will ideally be:

  • Exceptionally organised with strong attention to detail.

  • Proactive and able to anticipate what needs to happen next.

  • Comfortable managing multiple calendars and competing priorities.

  • Reliable and able to follow tasks through without needing frequent reminders.

Desirable Experience

The successful Personal Assistant will create order, visibility and peace of mind around the family’s day-to-day commitments.

Appointments are remembered, diaries remain coordinated, family members know where they need to be, important events aren’t missed, and practical tasks—from the car service to the vet appointment—are handled proactively and followed through to completion.

The role should ultimately reduce the mental load of running a busy personal and family life so the Operations Director can focus their attention where it is most needed.
