Headquarters: United States
URL: http://www.halcyon.ai

What we do:
Halcyon is the industry’s first dedicated, adaptive security platform that combines multiple proprietary advanced prevention engines along with AI models focused specifically on stopping ransomware.

Who we are:
Halcyon was formed in 2021 by a team of cyber industry veterans after battling the scourge of ransomware (and advanced threats) for years at some of the largest global security vendors. Comprised of leaders from Cylance (now Blackberry), Accuvant (now Optiv), Fireye and ISS X-Force (now IBM), Halcyon is focused on building products and solutions for mid-market and enterprise customers.

As a remote-native, completely distributed global team, we recognize great talent can exist anywhere. We invite you to apply to a job you’re interested in and we'll work a plan to meet your needs.

The Role  

  

At Halcyon, we’re building a world-class anti-ransomware platform grounded in innovation and resilience. As part of that vision, we’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our cloud team. You’ll lead the development and evolution of our data platform and API services, working within a modern tech stack that blends Scala and Rust.   

You’ll join a team focused on building scalable, maintainable backend systems that serve both internal and customer-facing functions. Your primary focus will be on Rust and Scala services, with opportunities to shape our transition to Rust where it makes sense. Python development experience is highly valued, particularly for supporting our security analysis platform which includes malware analysis engines, automated threat detection, and machine learning workflows.  

Responsibilities  

  • Lead the design and delivery of features across our data platform and public API services, including ingestion, transformation, and enrichment of security data. 
  • Drive system design, architecture, and data flow decisions in partnership with product and platform engineering. 
  • Build, deploy, and own Scala-based backend services in production, keeping them reliable, secure, and performant. 
  • Help shape and execute our migration of selected APIs from Scala to Rust, ensuring consistency and continuity along the way. 
  • Set the bar for code quality, documentation, and operational excellence.  
  • Lead design reviews, code reviews and take part in on-call and incident response. 
  • Support and enhance our Python-based security analysis platform, including malware analysis engines, automated threat detection, and machine learning model workflows.  

Skills and Qualifications  

  • 5+ years of backend engineering experience, with recent experience in a JVM-based codebase.  
  • A track record of designing and owning distributed systems from start to finish. 
  • Experience with Rust, or a well-formed view of when it’s the right tool, and the ability to help guide a migration. 
  • Strong understanding of APIs, messaging systems (Kafka), and modern data stores (Postgres, DynamoDB, OpenSearch).  
  • Experience building services in a cloud-native environment, preferably AWS.  
  • Working knowledge of containers and Kubernetes.  
  • Comfortable working in a remote-first, asynchronous team environment.  

Bonus Skills and Qualifications  

  • Familiarity with functional programming patterns and idiomatic Scala.  
  • Experience with Databricks and ClickHouse (or similar lakehouse and analytical/OLAP data stores). 
  • Experience with Terraform, Helm, and GitHub Actions.  
  • Familiarity with observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch).  
  • Prior work on security products, data pipelines, or high-availability systems.  
  • Python development experience, particularly with security analysis tools and malware detection frameworks (YARA, PE analysis, binary analysis).  
  • Familiarity with machine learning workflows, AutoML, and MLflow for model deployment and management.  
  • Experience with binary analysis libraries (LIEF, ssdeep, TLSH) and security tooling integration. 

Benefits:

 Halcyon offers the following benefits to eligible employees:

  • Comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, and vision) with premiums paid in full for employees and dependents.

  • 401k plan with a generous employer contribution.

  • Short and long-term disability coverage, basic life and AD&D insurance plans.

  • Medical and dependent care FSA options.

  • Flexible PTO policy.

  • Parental leave.

  • Generous equity offering.

The Company reserves the right to modify or change these benefits programs at any time, with or without notice.​

Base Salary Range: $120,000 - $170,000

Bonus Target: 10%

In accordance with applicable state and federal laws, the range provided is Halcyon’s reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. The actual amount may differ based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and location. Base pay is one part of the total package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and equity in the Company.

We understand it takes a diverse team of highly intelligent, passionate, curious, and creative people to develop the exceptional product we are building. Our dynamic team has incredible perspectives to share, just as we know you do, and we take great pride in being an equal opportunity employer.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/halcyon-senior-backend-cloud-engineer

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Greece
URL: https://jobs.workable.com/company/ssarktiaEdEzba97Jjs1YN/jobs-at-patchstack

Overview

Patchstack protects WordPress sites for hosts, agencies and developers, and we're now launching a security product for people building JavaScript apps with AI tools like Claude Code. That product is early. We have good signals from hosts and hackathons, but we haven't yet found who it serves best, what they value, or why they'll keep paying for it.

You'll be the product manager who finds that out. You'll talk to customers, use the product in real AI-assisted workflows, test ideas quickly with our designer and engineers, and build the measurement that tells us what's working. You'll work alongside two small engineering squads, a senior product designer, QA and infrastructure. You own which customer problems we invest in and how we learn from the results.

About you

You're happiest early, before the answers exist. You'd rather run a small test this week than wait for perfect data. You're comfortable in a terminal and have built things with AI-assisted tools, so you can use our product the way our customers do. You form your own view on technical claims rather than taking "it's not feasible" or "the metric improved" at face value. You say what you think, including when it's awkward, and you change your mind when the evidence says so. You work well in a flat team with little process, and you help people around you get better rather than taking work off them.

This is a fully remote job, based anywhere in Europe.

Responsibilities

  • Run customer discovery for the JavaScript product: interviews, observed usage, support and event feedback, and your own hands-on use.
  • With Growth and Product Marketing, recommend which customers and problems to focus on, backed by evidence of who uses, who pays and why.
  • Shape what we build with the Senior Product Designer from early discovery through testing. You own the problem and intended outcome; they own the design response.
  • Agree outcomes and priorities with the engineering squads and help them turn validated problems into work. Squads own delivery.
  • Build and ship small prototypes, experiments and product changes yourself where that's the fastest way to learn, within our review and QA process.
  • Own product measurement in PostHog: define the actions that matter, get tracking in place, and combine the numbers with customer evidence to explain what's working.
  • Keep what we've learned, decided and assumed visible in Notion so the team can make good investment calls.
  • Raise risks, gaps and decisions early, and escalate anything beyond your remit.
  • Experience as a product manager on a technical or developer-facing product, ideally pre or early product-market fit.
  • Examples of changing or stopping a product direction based on customer and technical evidence you gathered yourself.
  • Hands-on with AI-assisted development, the command line, packages and dependencies. You don't need to be a production engineer, but you need to be at home in that environment.
  • Strong customer research and data analysis skills, including building useful measurement from little reliable data.
  • Clear, direct communication with designers, engineers and leadership in a remote, low-process team.
  • €75–100k salary, depending on location and experience, plus company stock options
  • 4.5-day working week (half-day Fridays)
  • Remote-first, with reasonable overlap with EU timezones
  • 38 days' paid time off a year (including public holidays) plus 3 health days
  • Company laptop, and co-working membership or home-office equipment
  • AI tooling budget
  • Quarterly health and wellness allowance
  • Travel for conferences, events and our annual company meetup

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/patchstack-senior-product-manager

jobs.title: Revenue Cycle Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

We are fixing US healthcare by building an AI-native physical care platform, starting with home health.

Home health is a $140B industry with less than $10B in EBITDA â 40% of revenue is spent on pure administrative waste. We automate this work with AI, creating a fundamentally different cost structure compared to incumbents. This lets us rapidly take market share by serving the 30% of patients who go untreated today.

By reshaping the cost structure of this industry, we unlock its growth.

We've built one of the best AI teams in the world (from Character AI, Scale, Palantir, Citadel, Jane Street) and paired them with a team of healthcare veterans to build a new type of healthcare company: one that delivers care at the speed of an AI company.

Our physical care platform already operates with 30pp higher gross margins than traditional home health providers. With our AI advantage, we pay nurses more, remove their admin burden, and unlock the scale economics that have been missing from this fragmented industry. If we served this entire $140B market, instead of $10B in EBITDA, we'd drive $60B.

We're starting with home health, then expanding to all delivered care. Our mission is "any care, any where".

Fundamentally, our incentives are aligned with America. Every dollar in revenue we make is two dollars taken out of the healthcare system. If we succeed, so does US healthcare.

Role overview

Weâre seeking a hands-on Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) Manager to lead and support a team of specialists in a home health environment. This manager will stay close to daily operations, monitor team performance, and respond quickly to questions and emerging issues to help the team meet its goals. The role focuses on accounts receivable (AR), helping the team move outstanding claims from follow-up to verified resolution.

What Youâll Do

  • Manage and support RCM specialists working across home health revenue cycle workflows.

  • Track attendance and monitor individual and team performance against established KPIs and daily quotas.

  • Review workflow boards throughout the day to spot backlogs, red flags, and specialists at risk of missing their end-of-day quotas.

  • Respond promptly to specialist questions while balancing real-time workflow monitoring and other team needs.

  • Identify process gaps and work with the team to resolve issues affecting daily performance.

  • Apply your home health and Homecare Homebase (HCHB) knowledge to help specialists navigate workflows and resolve operational questions.

Accounts receivable and collections

  • Guide specialists and team leads in prioritizing assigned commercial, Medicare, and Medicare Advantage receivables, including aged balances, payer responses, rejections, denials, and upcoming filing or appeal deadlines.

  • Oversee claim follow-up through resolution: verify claim status and payment, investigate collection barriers and underpayments, and guide appropriate corrections, reprocessing, reconsiderations, or appeals under payer-specific requirements.

  • Review and respond to escalations when a specialist cannot determine the next action; surface recurring payer, workflow, or system issues to leadership and coordinate their resolution.

  • Ensure claim activity, supporting evidence, next actions, and follow-up dates are documented accurately in the applicable AR workflow and HCHB.

  • Partner with billing, payment posting, prior authorization, clinical, and other teams to resolve discrepancies, obtain documentation, and follow paid-but-not-posted claims through resolution.

  • Review proposed write-offs for documented collection efforts and supporting evidence, and route them through the required approval and posting process.

Quality and team development

  • Review claim work for accurate denial interpretation, appropriate action, complete documentation, timely follow-up, and correct escalation; use findings to coach specialists and strengthen performance.

  • Support onboarding, payer and system cross-training, and regular knowledge sharing. Identify patterns behind collection challenges and update SOPs or workflows to prevent repeat issues.

  • Share frontline feedback on AR dashboards and automation with relevant teams to improve prioritization, visibility, and specialist workflows.

Basic Qualifications

  • Strong experience in home health revenue cycle operations.

  • Familiarity with Homecare Homebase (HCHB).

  • Experience managing RCM specialists, including tracking attendance and performance KPIs.

  • Experience monitoring workflows throughout the day and identifying risks to daily productivity targets.

  • Experience identifying collection challenges and implementing processes to resolve.

  • Working knowledge of AR follow-up, denial investigation, appeals or reprocessing, and payer-specific filing requirements.

  • Experience reviewing claim documentation and quality, escalating unresolved issues, and coordinating with billing or posting teams.

  • Ability to respond promptly to team questions while managing multiple priorities.

  • Ability to identify workflow or process gaps and help the team address them.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing distributed or offshore revenue cycle teams.

  • Familiarity with commercial fee-for-service and Medicare or Medicare Advantage home health claims, including episodic/PDGM workflows.

  • Experience with AR dashboards, clearinghouses, and payer portals such as Waystar and Availity.

  • Experience using denial trends, quality reviews, or operational data to improve collections workflows and team training.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary

  • Comprehensive health insurance, dental, and commuter benefits

  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer contribution

  • Opportunity for growth in a fast-growing company

  • Collaborative team valuing innovation and problem-solving

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
About us

At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.

The role

Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer.

You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients.

You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list.

  • Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them.

  • Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs.

  • Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses.

  • Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path.

  • Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended.

  • Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them.

  • Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client.

  • Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse.

  • Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards.

  • Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need.

  • Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework.

Your background

You will have three to five years of product management experience, and you want to own a key product and take it to the next level. You might be a great fit if you can walk us through:

  • A product you grew from a small group of power users to broad adoption, and what you changed to get there.

  • Shipping a builder, automation or workflow tool, and what you learned about making something powerful easy to start with.

  • Building integrations with third-party platforms or APIs: how you chose which to build, and how you kept them working.

  • A time you built from validated customer need in a domain you had to go and learn. If your instinct is to start with a demo, this is not the role.

  • A decision you changed because the data told you to. Fluent in qual and quant.

  • Experience with AI agents or AI-assisted products is a plus.

You'll Thrive Here If Youâ¦

  • Move Fast. You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, iterating quickly, and fixing things before they become fires;

  • Stay Human. You care deeply about users and teammates, and design with empathy for real workflows;

  • Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just outputs. You spot problems early and take initiative to fix them.

  • Keep It Simple. You fight unnecessary complexity, design reusable patterns, and make hard things feel intuitive.

  • Love to Surprise. You enjoy finding unexpected ways to delight users, especially in the last mile of polish and usability.

KPIs & Success Measures

We will measure success through outcomes and quality, not just output:

  • Builder share (lead): percentage of monthly active users who build or edit a workflow. Target [TBD]%.

  • Workflow adoption (lead): percentage of monthly active users who run a workflow. Target [TBD]%.

  • Workflow run growth: month-on-month percentage growth in workflow runs. Target [TBD]%.

  • First workflow conversion: percentage of new users who complete a successful run within their first [TBD] days.

  • Share of generations through workflows: percentage of all generations produced by workflow runs.

  • Agent and human collaboration: percentage of workflow runs built or started by Scribble.

  • Connector adoption: percentage of active workspaces that use at least one third-party connection in a workflow each month. Target [TBD]%.

  • Integration usage: percentage of workflow runs that start from, or deliver to, a third-party connection. Target [TBD]%.

  • Reliability (hygiene bar): percentage of runs that complete without manual intervention, held at or above [TBD]%.

  • Learning velocity (supporting): percentage of launches reviewed after release against their stated hypothesis. Target 100%.

Benefits

  • 25 days PTO plus public holidays, although we operate a Flexible Time Off scheme

  • Health insurance / private medical cover

  • Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development

  • Remote - work from anywhere in your home country

  • Enhanced parental leave policies, whether you become a parent through birth, adoption or surrogacy

  • Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for our UK employees

  • Flexible working hours

Deep Dive About Pencil

Pencil uses AI to make ads. Our mission is to make marketing effective and effortless. We want to become the default way ads get made - because AI ads are 10x faster and cheaper to make, and 2x better performing, than making them without AI.

We're called Pencil because we believe AI will be a tool for creative people, not a replacement - it may even be as fundamental a tool in the future as the pencil was in the past.

Pencil was founded in 2018 with a team from Google, Facebook and Uber with backing from Sequoia and Entrepreneur First. We were acquired by The Brandtech Group in 2023 to pursue a shared vision of bringing GenAI to the Fortune 500.

https://www.trypencil.com

About The Brandtech Group

The Brandtech Group's mission is to be the best company in the world at helping leading global brands drive growth by connecting content, data and media using technology.

It was founded in June 2015 (as You & Mr Jones) by former Havas Global CEO David Jones, with a simple mission to help brands do their marketing better, faster and cheaper using technology. It was renamed The Brandtech Group in January 2022.

Today it generates more than $1BN in revenue and is the largest global digital content partner for many of the world's biggest brands and companies, often using its unique in-housing model. It works with eight of the world's top 10 global advertisers and 49 of the world's top 100. Clients include Banco ItaÃº, Danone, Google, Intuit, LVMH, Microsoft, Morgan-Stanley, Netflix, Reckitt, Renault-Nissan, PayPal, TikTok, Uber and Unilever.

In addition, the Group invests in cutting-edge technology companies relevant to and with potential in marketing and has been investing in the AI, AR and the metaverse space since 2015. The Group was the first external investor in Niantic (creators of PokÃ©mon Go), alongside investments in AI Foundation (AI digital twins, personalized AI, and deep-fake detection 2018), Automat (AI chatbots, 2016), Elsy (AI media planning, 2016), Jivox (dynamic automated content, 2016), Crossing Minds (deep learning AI recommendation system, 2017), CreativeX (AI-driven content optimization, 2022), Zappar (AR, 2017), Provenance (blockchain, 2022) and GGP (the world's largest gaming fund).

The Group is one of the most prominent marketing industry voices on the prediction and movement to AI-driven marketing, including Generative AI. It was named one of the World's Most Innovative Companies 2021 by Fast Company, and by CB Insights as one of the World's Most Valuable Private Unicorns.

https://www.thebrandtechgroup.com

RainFocus, one of the most innovative software companies, is in search of an exceptional Jr. UI Developer.

 

About RainFocus

RainFocus cares about its employees, customers, and the world in which we live. Our rapidly growing team serves Fortune 500 companies like Adobe, Cisco, IBM, Oracle, VMware, and others to prepare and execute in-person, virtual, and hybrid events, across the world. Those events are delivered through our industry-disrupting software platform, with groundbreaking business intelligence, to elevate the attendee experience, streamline event operations, and accelerate marketing results. We are well-funded, growing fast, and building a company that is changing the market â it will be challenging, fun and exciting. 

 

About the Role

As a Jr. UI Developer, you will be an essential part of our team, assisting in the implementation of stunning, user-friendly web applications. Working alongside experienced developers, you will use HTML, CSS, and modern JavaScript to help translate designs into high-quality web experiences for our events and platforms. This position is ideal for an early-career developer who is passionate about visually-focused development, eager to learn best practices in CSS and JavaScript, and excited to collaborate within a supportive team environment. You will gain hands-on experience with branding, workflows, and enterprise-grade software development.

\n


How you will contribute:

  • Assist in developing, updating, and maintaining UI components and branding with a strong focus on design and responsiveness.

  • Collaborate closely with senior developers, designers, and Product Management to learn processes and deliver quality work.

  • Write clean, maintainable HTML, CSS (using SASS and utility classes), and basic JavaScript (including exposure to React and Svelte).

  • Help troubleshoot, debug, and fix styling issues or UI-related bugs across different browsers and devices.

  • Participate in code reviews to receive feedback, learn RainFocus coding standards, and improve your skills.

  • Support the team in configuring client white-labeling, templates, and basic event workflows.


Required Experience/ Skills:

  • 1â2 years of professional web development experience, or equivalent experience through bootcamps, internships, or robust portfolio projects.

  • Solid fundamental knowledge of HTML, CSS, and CSS preprocessors like SASS.

  • Basic understanding of vanilla JavaScript and an eagerness to learn modern frameworks like React and Svelte.

  • Understanding of responsive design principles and cross-browser compatibility.

  • Familiarity with version control systems, such as Git.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • A proactive mindset, self-motivated to ask questions, learn, and grow as a developer.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Works well in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

  • Exposure to design tools such as Figma, Adobe XD, or Photoshop.

  • Basic awareness of web accessibility (WCAG) standards.

  • Familiarity with Agile software development methodologies.

  • General understanding of how APIs or backend systems (like Java) interact with front-end code.


\n

Why work at RainFocus?

At RainFocus we delight millions of attendees at large-scale events by delivering better insights, experiences, and marketing. We were able to pivot our product and services offering in 2020 to continue growing and serving new clients and events.

 

As a member of the RainFocus team, you will have the opportunity to experience first-hand the impact of our platform at events around the world. Additionally, RainFocus offers competitive salaries, competitive benefits, 401k, generous PTO, and countless other team building activities. 

 

What are you waiting for? Apply today! We need more talented, hard-working, fun-loving team members just like yourself!

jobs.title: Instructional Designer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Sacramento, California, United States
URL: https://www.vituity.com/about-us/practice-management

Remote, Nationwide – Seeking Instructional Designer

 

Everybody Has A Role To Play In Transforming Healthcare

 

At Vituity you are part of a larger team that is driven by our purpose to improve lives. We are dedicated to transforming healthcare through our culture by working together to tackle healthcare’s most pressing challenges from the inside.

 

Join the Vituity Team. At Vituity we’ve cultivated an environment where passion thrives, and success comes through shared purpose. We were founded in a culture that values team accomplishments more than individual achievements, an approach we call “culture of brilliance.” Together, we leverage our strengths and experiences to make a positive impact in our local communities. We foster this through shared goals and helping our colleagues succeed, and we also understand the importance of recognition, taking the time to show appreciation and gratitude for a job well done.

 

Vituity Locations: Vituity has opportunities at 900 practices across the country, serving 14.5+ million patients a year. With Vituity, if you ever need to move, you can take your job with you.

 

The Opportunity

  • Designs and develops engaging, accessible, learner-centered learning solutions that support enterprise education, organizational initiatives, knowledge transfer, and performance.
  • Conducts learning and performance analyses to identify audience needs, desired performance, root causes, skill gaps, and appropriate learning or performance-support solutions.
  • Develops and customizes learning across modalities, including eLearning, instructor-led and virtual learning, blended programs, job aid, microlearning, simulations, assessments, video, communications, and other performance-support resources.
  • Translates complex content into clear, accurate, engaging, and learner-centered experiences through research and collaboration with SMEs and stakeholders.
  • Develops measurable learning objectives, instructional strategies, storyboards, scripts, prototypes, practice activities, assessments, and evaluation approaches aligned to intended performance outcomes.
  • Applies instructional design and adult-learning principles, learning science, usability, accessibility, content governance, brand/design standards; uses approved AI-enabled tools responsibly to support analysis, design, development, and quality assurance.
  • Conducts quality assurance and user testing to identify and resolve content, accessibility, usability, and functionality issues before implementation.
  • Creates and edits multimedia assets and refreshes, improves, or retires learning assets based on feedback, data, content changes, and business needs.
  • Shares design approaches, tools, lessons learned, and work in progress to support team learning and consistency.
  • Participates in peer reviews and provides timely, constructive, and actionable feedback; seeks and incorporates feedback on their own work.
  • Applies established instructional design standards and contributes recommendations to improve templates, guidance, workflows, and best practices.
  • Independently manages assigned learning projects, including scope, timelines, milestones, stakeholder reviews, approvals, dependencies, risks, and deliverables.
  • Balances multiple projects and competing priorities while maintaining quality, responsiveness, and alignment with agreed-upon requirements.
  • Identifies opportunities to improve learning experiences, development processes, tools, templates, and team workflows.
  • Evaluates and uses approved learning technologies, automation, and AI-enabled tools to improve quality, efficiency, and learner experience.
  • Contributes instructional design and digital-content expertise to pilots, cross-functional projects, technology testing, and improvement initiatives within assigned scope.
  • Partners with SMEs and stakeholders to clarify performance needs, desired outcomes, audience requirements, and project expectations.
  • Recommends appropriate learning, performance support, or non-training solutions based on identified needs and constraints.
  • Provides guidance on learning strategy, modality selection, learner experience, accessibility, and implementation considerations.
  • Communicates recommendations, tradeoffs, progress, risks, and decisions clearly to stakeholders.
  • Builds productive relationships with internal partners and represents Learning & Development professionally.
  • May manage solely, or in partnership with the LMS Administrator, including but not limited to: uploading, testing, updating, maintaining, and retiring courses and curricula in accordance with established standards and processes.
  • Troubleshoots course-level Learning Management System (LMS) issues related to functionality, navigation, tracking, completion, and learner experience; supports testing of Learning Management System (LMS) updates and features and escalate system-level issues to the Learning Management System (LMS) Administrator as appropriate.
  • Partners with the Learning Management System (LMS) Administrator and stakeholders to support learner assignments and course delivery and develops or maintains SOPs and documentation related to instructional design processes and Learning Management System (LMS) interactions as needed.

 

Required Experience and Competencies

  • Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, education, business, communications, or a related field required OR an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.
  • 2+ years of experience in instructional design or learning content development, with related experience in areas such as technical writing/editing, digital content, multimedia development, or content governance required.

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required

  • 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.
  • Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.
  • Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.
  • Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.
  • You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.
  • Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.
  • Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.
  • Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have

  • Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.
  • Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.
  • Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.
  • Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.
  • Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

How we work and what we offer

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

What we offer:

  • A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software
  • Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

jobs.description:
ð Build the data layer AI needs to do science

Application deadline: 16 Nov 2026 23:59 CET

About Claims

AI ate the Internet, but it can't digest science yet. A paper is thousands of words of prose written for humans, but an AI agent doing research needs to know what was claimed, what evidence supports it, and how far to trust it. Claims turns the scientific literature into exactly that: every claim, tied to its evidence, as structured data that models and agents can query.

We're a startup and run as Subnet 111 on Bittensor. Since our mainnet launch on 28 August 2026, an open competition of miners has processed more than 10,000 papers, and every record was checked by our validator before it entered the dataset. The competition keeps raising the bar: miners keep finding ways to beat our own reference pipeline, and every win becomes part of the standard the whole network is scored against.

The team

Claims was founded by two professors of economics and a senior engineer.

  • Philipp Koellinger, CEO, is a professor of economics and an experienced entrepreneur: founder of DeSci Labs and the DeSci Foundation, and co-builder of SciWeave with Ogban.
  • Christian Roessler, co-founder, is a professor of economics and game theorist. He designs the incentive mechanism that makes the miner competition work.
  • Ogban Ugot, engineering, is a senior backend and machine learning engineer. He built SciWeave, the Claims miner, validator and data pipeline, and you will work with him every day.

You would be the fourth person on the team and our second engineer.

Our culture

We are a fully remote team spread across Europe, Africa and the US West Coast. We have a flat hierarchy and move fast towards clearly defined goals. We think deep, don't shy away from difficult problems or conversations, and we ship relentlessly. The code you will write will run on a live network within your first weeks, and you own real things from day one. We are an AI-native company and expect you to be an AI-native Software Engineer we can trust.

About the role

Position: Software Engineer (Python, full-stack)
Location: Remote. You need to be able to join our team meetings in the afternoon, Central European Time.
Type: Full-time contractor. Start in December 2026 or January 2027.

We're looking for a Software Engineer to help maintain and build Claims and its supporting applications, services, and developer tools. Claims turns scientific research into structured claims and supporting evidence through document processing, AI pipelines, and automated evaluation.

This is a hands-on, backend-focused full-stack role. You'll work across Python services, web dashboards, data pipelines, integrations, and deployment tooling. Your work will combine delivering new features with debugging existing systems, improving reliability, and making the codebase easier to maintain.

You should be comfortable owning well-defined tasks from investigation through implementation, testing, and release, working with the team on larger design decisions and unfamiliar areas.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain Python backend services, APIs, command-line tools, and background processing workflows.
  • Develop and improve web dashboards and internal review tools using TypeScript, React, and modern web frameworks.
  • Maintain pipelines that ingest research papers, process documents, extract structured information, and evaluate results.
  • Integrate external APIs and AI model providers, handling validation, retries, timeouts, rate limits, and usage costs.
  • Work with relational databases and object storage, including schema changes, migrations, queries, and data integrity checks.
  • Investigate bugs and production issues across services, pipelines, and interfaces; address root causes and add useful regression coverage.
  • Help maintain deployment automation, continuous integration, logging, monitoring, and operational documentation.
  • Improve existing code through practical refactoring, dependency maintenance, automated tests, and code review.
  • Collaborate with engineering and research colleagues to turn requirements and experimental workflows into reliable software.

Required skills and experience

  • Typically 1â5 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience delivering and maintaining production software.
  • Strong Python skills, including building maintainable services or data processing applications, managing dependencies, and writing automated tests.
  • Experience designing, consuming, and troubleshooting HTTP APIs, with a sound understanding of JSON, validation, authentication, and error handling.
  • Working knowledge of TypeScript or JavaScript and experience contributing to React applications or a comparable modern frontend framework.
  • Practical SQL and relational database experience, including data modelling, migrations, and debugging queries.
  • Confidence working in Linux environments and using the command line to investigate logs, configuration, processes, and service failures.
  • Experience with Git, pull requests, code review, automated testing, and continuous integration.
  • An understanding of secure engineering practices, including access controls, secrets management, and careful handling of private data.
  • The ability to navigate an existing codebase, trace issues across components, and make focused, well-tested changes.
  • Clear communication, practical problem-solving, and the judgment to work independently while asking for input when requirements or risks are unclear.

Nice to have

  • Experience with FastAPI, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Next.js, or similar tools.
  • Experience integrating LLM APIs, building AI-assisted workflows, or evaluating model outputs for accuracy, reliability, latency, and cost.
  • Familiarity with PDF parsing, OCR, document extraction, scientific datasets, or evidence provenance.
  • Experience with distributed jobs, asynchronous processing, reproducible pipelines, or automated benchmarking.
  • Familiarity with Docker, Ansible, systemd, GitHub Actions, cloud hosting, or infrastructure automation.
  • Experience with Bittensor, decentralized compute networks, or systems for evaluating independently submitted code.
  • Exposure to Rust, native Python extensions, or WebAssembly.
  • An interest in scientific research, open-source software, and tools that make research easier to inspect and reuse.

You don't need experience with every technology listed. Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to learn quickly across the stack matter most.

What success looks like

  • You can independently deliver scoped features and fixes across the backend and supporting web applications.
  • Your changes are understandable, tested, and documented, with appropriate attention to security and compatibility.
  • You help make processing pipelines and production services more reliable and easier to troubleshoot.
  • You contribute constructively to reviews, communicate progress and blockers, and help the team turn research ideas into maintainable software.

What we offer

  • $1500 - $2000 per month, depending on experience.
  • Opportunities for rapid professional growth in a high-impact role: a small team, a live network, and a senior engineer to learn from.
  • Quarterly team retreats in inspiring locations (e.g., Vilnius, Koh Samui).
  • Travel and visa support for business needs.
  • Flexible remote working.


Help us build the data layer that lets AI do science properly.

How to apply


Apply online through the link here: https://airtable.com/appZKkV7FT7eYBhKI/shrjJ3jYfxZjsNckR

It takes about 30 minutes: a few practical questions, four short written answers, links to your code, and your CV or personal website. No cover letter needed.

Are you a product driven problem solver who enjoys turning customer insight into things that actually get built? Do you love turning complexity into clarity, aligning teams, and shaping product experiences that genuinely make people’s lives easier? If so, we’d love to meet you!

We build software that takes the stress, chaos, and friction out of managing a health practice. As our newest Product Owner, you’ll play a pivotal role in translating vision into action, turning customer needs into features and driving product outcomes that truly matter.

You’re someone on the rise - intelligent, opinionated (in the best way), and ready to make an impact. You’re not easily swayed, and you’re happy to take a stand when it serves the customer and the product. You connect dots, ask great questions, and care deeply about delivering value. Everything we build helps health professionals spend less time on admin and more time helping patients. Your work will directly improve lives.
✅ Competitive Pay

About the role

Descript's script-based editing features are at the heart of why creators trust us for their highest-stakes content. Product launches. Client interviews. Marketing campaigns. Content that represents them to their audiences.

As Lead Product Manager of the Narrative Editing team, you'll own how users capture, edit, and perfect their stories. You'll shape the script-first editing that makes video as simple as a document, the recording and writing tools that let users create without leaving Descript, and the AI regeneration features that make edits feel seamless and natural.

This is an opportunity to shape features that professional creators depend on while working with cutting-edge AI, a product users love, and a small, collaborative team where your impact is immediate and visible.

What you’ll do

  • Develop a deep understanding of our customers, their creative goals, and the evolving AI video landscape — and use those insights to guide the editor roadmap
  • Bring Descript's taste for great video into interactions and defaults, so creators naturally produce polished, professional work
  • Continuously expand our editing capabilities with frontier AI technology by partnering with our AI Research team, launching features like video regeneration and automatic speaker identification
  • Own the recording, script generation, and translation flows that help users achieve their end-to-end video workflows directly in Descript
  • Ensure Descript scales reliably for larger teams and more complex workflows

Who you are

  • You’ve built deceptively powerful tools: You have 5 or more years of product management experience shipping creative tools or workflow products that feel simple enough for everyone, but scale to handle sophisticated use cases. You are a systems-minded product thinker who excels at designing intuitive experiences for complex, end-to-end workflows.
  • You start with the customer: Plenty of “AI products” start with the technology and they all suck. You care deeply about understanding customers, and have experience in doing customer discovery and defining features that solve real problems.
  • You are a fog sculptor: There are aspects to our editor and its design that do not have real competitors yet. The product intuition and design conventions have not been decided. You are attracted to ambiguous problems, know how to ask smart questions, and translate ideas into action.
  • You care about craft: Our product is not a hype machine that runs on empty promises and vaporware. We think our product will be successful because people love to use it. That means you sweat the details. But without the sweat, because you aren’t stressed out.
  • You are funny, creative, maybe kind of weird: Ok, this isn’t a hard requirement but Descript is kind of a quirky place and the people who love it tend to like that about working here. So, just want to drop a hint early on. Also, the sense of humor is important because even though we take our work seriously it’s still just, like, video creation and editing. We aren’t flying rockets into space so let’s all have a good time.

The base salary range for this role is $225,000 - $290,000. Final offer amounts will carefully consider multiple factors, including prior experience, expertise, location, level, and may vary from the amount above.

About Descript

Descript is building a simple, intuitive, fully-powered editing tool for video and audio — an editing tool built for the age of AI. We are a team of 150 and the backing of some of the world's greatest investors (OpenAI, Andreessen Horowitz, Redpoint Ventures, Spark Capital). 

Descript is the special company that's in possession of both product market fit and the raw materials (passionate user community, great product, large market) for growth, but is still early enough that each new employee has a measurable influence on the direction of the company.

Benefits include a generous healthcare package, 401k matching program, catered lunches, and flexible vacation time. Our headquarters are located in the Mission District of San Francisco, CA. We're hiring for a mix of remote roles and hybrid roles.  For those who are remote, we have a handful of opportunities throughout the year for in person collaboration.  For our hybrid roles, we're flexible, and you're an adult—we don't expect or mandate that you're in the office every day. We do believe there are valuable and serendipitous moments of discovery and collaboration that come from working together in person. 

Descript is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. jobs.title: Software Engineer Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Software Engineer, Infrastructure

Hybrid in Palo Alto (Mon / Wed / Thurs) Â· $185Kâ$215K base + meaningful early-stage equity + full benefits

Â 

About Sodalis

Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait.

Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist.

We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx).

Â 

The Opportunity

Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own.
We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live.

We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range.
You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture.

What you'll do

  • Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between.

  • Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy.

  • Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site.

  • Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range.

  • Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering.

  • You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services.

  • You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded.

  • You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them.

  • You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity.

  • You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required.

How we work

We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk.

Join our growing team and help shape the future of homebuying! To learn more, visit Knock.com

Lending Manager (Front End)

About the role

Knock is looking for an experienced mortgage leader to manage and grow our team of fully remote Loan Assistants. This is a 100% remote role, and you’ll lead a team distributed across the country. You enjoy building teams, finding efficiencies, and using technology to improve how work gets done. You’re approachable, open-minded, and adaptable. You know the work well enough to coach it and you’re willing to jump in and help. In this role you’ll own the Loan Assistant and post-closing pipelines, develop your team, and work with the Director of Lending Operations to make our processes better.

jobs.title: Scientific Account Executive
jobs.description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

Weâre growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers â from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.

The day-to-day:

  • Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

  • Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform

  • Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results

  • Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected

  • Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts â new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management.

  • Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity).

  • Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means.

  • Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly.

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs.

  • Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns.

  • Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures.

  • Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals.

What we're looking for

  • Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up.

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role: field application scientist, technical sales, scientific account management, or similar. CRO or biotech vendor experience is a strong plus.

  • Commercially driven. You care about revenue, pipeline, and closing deals, not just having interesting scientific conversations.

  • Strong communicator who can adapt to the audience: detailed and technical with a scientist, concise and business-focused with a VP.

  • Self-starter who can manage their own pipeline and priorities without heavy oversight.

  • Genuine interest in AI-driven protein design and the companies working in this space. You follow what's happening in the field.

Application deadline

jobs.title: Autonomous Systems Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote-Friendly (Travel Required) | San Francisco, CA

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. You'll be the engineer who owns autonomous systems across that footprint as one security domain, from both sides: drones, ground robots and automated vehicles for patrol, inspection and moving hardware, including the security of that automation inside secure areas, and the detection systems that tell us what is flying over or operating near a site uninvited.

You set the approach, select and integrate the platforms and sensors, write the requirements vendors build to, and run what you ship, from the operating model where operators assign missions and machines carry them out to the playbook that turns a detection into an identified track and a well-evidenced handoff to whoever holds authority over the airspace. Interdiction is not part of this role. The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, fleet health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well.

You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations and legal teams, and directly with site operators, equipment vendors and aviation and public safety authorities. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure.

Key responsibilities

  • Autonomous security and inspection systems: own the drones, ground robots and other autonomous platforms for perimeter patrol, incident response and infrastructure inspection: platform selection, operating model, operator qualification, maintenance, and the data path from machine to analyst

  • Tools, automation and AI agents: build the integrations that carry detections, tracks, telemetry and fleet health into the team's security monitoring platform, and the tools and agents that triage detections, check fleet health and assemble evidence. When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it

  • Detection of uncrewed systems: engineer the sensing that tells us what is flying over or operating near a site, what it is and who needs to know: sensor selection and evaluation against live targets, per-site coverage, classification and false-alarm handling, and the playbook from first detection to handoff, with evidence retained

  • Security of site automation: engineer the controls on automated vehicles, robots and similar machines that move hardware or work inside secure areas: identity and access, network isolation, what they may record and where it goes, fail-secure behavior, their place in chain of custody, and acceptance before they enter a site

  • Regulatory and site constraints: establish what we may sense, fly, drive, record and retain at each site, partner-operated sites included, under the aviation, spectrum, privacy and safety rules that apply there, with the waivers and approvals that extend it and coordination with local authorities set up before it is needed

  • Health monitoring: define and test heartbeats, loss-of-coverage and lost-link alarms and fail-secure behavior, so a silent sensor or machine shows as a fault, not a quiet day

  • Vendor requirements and acceptance: write the requirements, evaluate against live flights and runs, and hold vendors to what they ship

Minimum qualifications

  • Have engineered autonomous or sensing systems in the field (drones, ground robots, automated vehicles, or RF, radar or optical detection sensors): selected, integrated or secured them for an operation other people relied on, and verified what they actually do against real targets or runs rather than a datasheet

  • Have integrated systems you did not build (vendor APIs, SDKs, appliances, machine and sensor telemetry) into a platform that outlives any one of them

  • Read and review code, design the data systems behind security tooling, and build automation (often with AI coding agents) using Git and code review

  • Have done this work hands-on for data centers, critical infrastructure or a large hardware fleet

  • Have designed inside a regulatory or safety constraint (aviation, spectrum, privacy, machine safety or similar) and can show the decision it drove

  • Own a domain end to end: set the approach, carry it through with vendors, site operators, partners and authorities, and run it as something people depend on every day

Preferred qualifications

  • Remote pilot certification (for example FAA Part 107) and experience flying beyond visual line of sight under a waiver or exemption

  • Experience with counter-drone (counter-UAS) detection, airspace surveillance or air traffic data systems

  • Experience running a robot, drone or automated-vehicle fleet in an industrial, logistics or data center setting: fleet management, mission planning, safety cases

  • Experience securing embedded, operational technology or robotic systems: device identity, network segmentation, update control, logging

  • Experience with physical security operations at large sites, with law enforcement or aviation authorities, or at sites you did not fully control: cloud, colocation or GPU cloud operators

  • Have built AI agents or automation that replaced recurring manual work

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$320,000—$405,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Keeper is hiring a detail-oriented Creative Localization Specialist to manage the localization of global creative assets across multiple languages and design platforms. This is a 100% remote position from select locations, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the Chicago, IL metro area.

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and is sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help deliver high-quality creative experiences to a global audience.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.

About the Role

As a Creative Localization Specialist, you will adapt existing creative assets into multiple languages and formats while ensuring accuracy, consistency, and adherence to Keeper’s brand and design standards. Reporting to the Director of Localization, you will work closely with the design team and Head of Product Design to manage localization workflows, resolve design challenges, and deliver polished assets across print, digital, and motion formats.

Responsibilities

  • Manage design localization workflows by submitting translation requests through Smartling and applying completed translations to Figma and other design files
  • Adapt layouts, spacing, formatting, and visual elements to accommodate language-specific text expansion and contraction
  • Maintain consistency in terminology, brand guidelines, formatting, and design standards across localized assets
  • Conduct quality assurance reviews to confirm accuracy, formatting, visual integrity, and overall design quality
  • Support the localization of digital, print, presentation, video, and other creative materials
  • Manage localization workflows, timelines, file handoffs, and deliverables across multiple languages and file types

  • Track project status and communicate updates, risks, and outstanding needs to relevant stakeholders
  • Support continuous improvements to localization processes, templates, and production workflows
  • Participate in special projects for the Localization, Design, and Product Design teams

  • Proficiency in Adobe InDesign and Figma

  • Experience working with localization workflows and multilingual design best practices
  • Ability to work accurately with translated content across multiple languages

  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Strong organizational and project management skills
  • Ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and file types simultaneously
